title: TBD LBD: The nature of `little blue dots'
comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, submitted. Comments are welcome
summary: Previous Sirocco radiative-transfer models of gas-cocooned AGN predicted lower-column counterparts to little red dots (LRDs): compact, X-ray-weak sources with bluer continuum slopes and Balmer jumps rather than Balmer breaks. The recently identified population of little blue dots (LBDs) closely resembles this predicted phase. Here we explore these lower-column-density cocoons in which nebular recombination emission remains visible while strong Balmer-continuum absorption is avoided. We find that a sequence of increasing column density connects more classical AGN spectra, Balmer-jump LBD-like spectra at $N_{\rm H}\!\sim\!{\rm few}\times10^{24} \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, and Balmer-break LRD-like spectra at higher columns. In this sequence, electron scattering produces exponential line wings and suppresses X-ray emission before strong Balmer absorption features, characteristic of higher column densities, appear. We therefore propose that LBDs are lower-column analogues of LRDs within a common gas-cocooned AGN sequence. This interpretation predicts that Balmer-jump emission, X-ray weakness, permitted lines with exponential wings, He II $λ$4686 emission, smaller H$α$ FWHM values and equivalent widths than in LRDs, and weak or absent absorption features are characteristic of LBDs. We compare to three example LBD spectra and identify Balmer-jump signatures in them.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that little blue dots (LBDs) are lower-column-density analogs of little red dots (LRDs) within a unified gas-cocooned AGN sequence, where increasing column density transitions from classical AGN to Balmer-jump LBDs to Balmer-break LRDs, with electron scattering suppressing X-rays and producing exponential line wings before strong Balmer absorption appears.
AI.motivation: To explain the recently identified population of little blue dots (LBDs) and connect them to previously predicted lower-column counterparts of little red dots (LRDs) in the gas-cocooned AGN framework.
AI.method: Sirocco radiative-transfer models of gas-cocooned AGN exploring a sequence of increasing column density from classical AGN through LBD-like (NH ~ few × 10^24 cm^-2) to LRD-like spectra, with comparison to three example LBD spectra.
AI.result: A sequence exists where increasing column density connects classical AGN → Balmer-jump LBDs → Balmer-break LRDs. Electron scattering produces exponential line wings and suppresses X-rays before strong Balmer absorption appears at higher columns. Balmer-jump signatures are identified in three example LBD spectra.
AI.conclusion: LBDs are lower-column analogues of LRDs within a common gas-cocooned AGN sequence, predicting characteristic features including Balmer-jump emission, X-ray weakness, permitted lines with exponential wings, He II λ4686 emission, smaller Hα FWHM and EW than LRDs, and weak/absent absorption features.

title: Unification models of Active Galactic Nuclei
comment: Invited chapter for the Encyclopedia of Astrophysics (edited by I. Mandel, section editor S. McGee) to be published by Elsevier as a Reference Module
summary: This chapter presents an overview of the unification models for Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), focusing on the physical structures, classification schemes, and evolutionary processes that characterize accreting supermassive black holes. We introduce the fundamental components of AGN, including the supermassive black hole, accretion disk, jets, outflows, broad-line and narrow-line regions, polar dust and the dusty anisotropic obscurer. The traditional orientation-based unification model is reviewed, with a focus on the role of the covering factor of the obscuring material in shaping observed properties. We introduce the radiation-regulated unification model, which accounts for the influence of radiative feedback on the nuclear environment of SMBHs. We also examine the evolutionary aspects of AGN unification, including the impact of galaxy mergers, host galaxy properties, and redshift-dependent trends. Finally, we discuss changing-look AGN, which challenge conventional unification frameworks by exhibiting dramatic spectral variability.

AI.tldr: This chapter reviews AGN unification models, covering physical structures (SMBH, accretion disk, jets, outflows, BLR/NLR, polar dust, obscurer), orientation-based unification with obscurer covering factors, radiation-regulated unification via radiative feedback, evolutionary aspects (mergers, host properties, redshift trends), and changing-look AGN that challenge standard unification.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of AGN unification models, addressing both the traditional orientation-based paradigm and newer radiation-regulated and evolutionary frameworks, while highlighting challenges from changing-look AGN.
AI.method: Literature review synthesizing observational and theoretical work on AGN structure, classification, orientation-based unification (covering factor of obscuring material), radiation-regulated unification (radiative feedback effects), evolutionary unification (mergers, host galaxies, redshift dependence), and changing-look AGN variability analysis.
AI.result: The orientation-based model explains many observed AGN types via viewing angle and covering factor; radiation-regulated unification adds radiative feedback as a key determinant of nuclear environment; evolutionary unification connects AGN phases to galaxy mergers, host properties, and cosmic epoch; changing-look AGN reveal dramatic spectral state transitions that challenge static unification frameworks.
AI.conclusion: AGN unification requires a multi-dimensional approach combining orientation, radiation feedback, and evolutionary effects; changing-look AGN demonstrate that unification models must account for temporal variability and state transitions in accretion flows.

title: Bar-induced migration of $ω$ Centauri away from Gaia Sausage-Enceladus
summary: The globular cluster $ω$ Cen has been suggested to have originated in the Gaia Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) merger event, possibly as its nuclear star cluster. However, the present-day orbits of $ω$ Cen and the GSE debris are very different. We investigate the scenario in which $ω$ Cen originated in the GSE and migrated to its current position due to perturbations from the Galactic bar. The [$α$/M] distributions of stars located between the GSE debris and $ω$ Cen in $(L_z,E)$ space tentatively support this scenario, but are not conclusive. We run simulations of the GSE debris and $ω$ Cen in a realistic Milky Way potential with a decelerating bar at various present-day pattern speeds. We find that $ω$ Cen can indeed be traced back to the phase space region occupied by the GSE debris. However, this likely requires a pattern speed of $Ω_\mathrm{b}\lesssim26$ km s$^{-1}$ kpc$^{-1}$, which is much lower than most recent estimates. We conclude that a GSE origin for $ω$ Cen is dynamically and chemically plausible, but this would require a re-evaluation of the current consensus on the bar's pattern speed.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether the globular cluster ω Cen originated in the Gaia Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) merger event and later migrated to its current position due to perturbations from the Galactic bar. Simulations show this is dynamically plausible but require a bar pattern speed ≤26 km s⁻¹ kpc⁻¹, much lower than current estimates, challenging the consensus on bar pattern speed.
AI.motivation: To test the hypothesis that ω Cen originated as the nuclear star cluster of the GSE merger event, despite its present-day orbit being very different from GSE debris, by examining whether Galactic bar perturbations could have caused its migration.
AI.method: Analysis of [α/M] distributions in (L_z, E) space, combined with N-body simulations of GSE debris and ω Cen in a realistic Milky Way potential with a decelerating Galactic bar at various pattern speeds.
AI.result: ω Cen can be traced back to the GSE debris phase space region, but this requires a bar pattern speed Ω_b ≲ 26 km s⁻¹ kpc⁻¹, significantly lower than most recent observational estimates.
AI.conclusion: A GSE origin for ω Cen is dynamically and chemically plausible, but it would necessitate re-evaluating the current consensus on the Milky Way bar's pattern speed.

title: The Hubble Missing Globular Clusters Survey IV. Ultra-faint compact satellites of the Milky Way. The case of Koposov 2
comment: 16 pages, 13 figures, submitted to A&A. Comments are welcome
summary: In the last decades a number of extremely faint and compact Galactic satellites (Ultra Faint Compact Satellites; UFCS) have been discovered by large panoramic surveys. Their nature is uncertain due to their location in the overlapping dwarf galaxy-star cluster region of the $M_V-R_h$ plane and their faintness and distance. Here we show how the deep HST photometry from the Missing Globular Clusters Survey (MGCS), combined with spectroscopic metallicities, provides new insight into the nature of these satellites through accurate distance and age estimates. We consider the case of Koposov 2, currently the most metal-poor bound star cluster known in the entire Milky Way or an extreme case of Ultra Faint Dwarf galaxy. By performing a spectroscopically-informed bayesian isochrone fit on the MGCS data we find $(m-M)_0=16.85\pm 0.06$ ($D=23.4\pm 0.6$ kpc) and age=$13.7^{+0.9}_{-1.3}$ Gyr, showing that, contrary to previous age estimates, Koposov 2 is as old as the oldest Galactic globular clusters. The luminosity function, corrected for incompleteness, is well reproduced by a model with the same age and metallicity and a slope of the mass function $x=-0.35$, suggesting a significant depletion of faint stars. We model the surface stellar density field, deriving new robust estimates of the half-light radius ($R_h=0.39^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ arcsec, corresponding to $R_h=2.7^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$ pc), of the absolute integrated magnitude ($M_V=-0.95\pm0.22$) and of the stellar mass ($M_{\star}=371.8\pm41.6M_{\odot}$), showing that Koposov 2 is much more compact than dwarf galaxies of similar stellar mass. The new evidence significantly support the hypothesis that Koposov 2 is a star cluster that may have lost a large fraction of its original mass. Finally we show that most UFCS lie in the same locus of the $M_V - R_h$ plane as Galactic open clusters, hinting to a possible additional channel for their formation.

AI.tldr: This paper uses deep HST photometry and spectroscopic metallicities to study Koposov 2, an ultra-faint compact satellite, finding it is an ancient (13.7 Gyr), metal-poor star cluster at 23.4 kpc, much more compact than dwarf galaxies of similar mass, supporting its classification as a star cluster that likely lost significant mass, with most UFCS occupying the same region as Galactic open clusters in the MV-Rh plane.
AI.motivation: The nature of Ultra Faint Compact Satellites (UFCS) is uncertain because they lie in the overlapping region between dwarf galaxies and star clusters in the MV-Rh plane, and their faintness and distance make characterization difficult.
AI.method: Spectroscopically-informed Bayesian isochrone fitting on deep HST photometry from the Missing Globular Clusters Survey (MGCS), combined with surface stellar density modeling and luminosity function analysis corrected for incompleteness.
AI.result: Koposov 2 has distance D=23.4±0.6 kpc, age=13.7+0.9-1.3 Gyr, half-light radius Rh=2.7+0.4-0.3 pc, MV=-0.95±0.22, stellar mass M⋆=371.8±41.6 M⊙, and a mass function slope x=-0.35 indicating significant depletion of low-mass stars.
AI.conclusion: Koposov 2 is as old as the oldest Galactic globular clusters, much more compact than dwarf galaxies of similar mass, supporting its classification as a star cluster that likely lost significant mass. Most UFCS occupy the same locus as Galactic open clusters in the MV-Rh plane, suggesting a possible additional formation channel.

title: Observing Cosmic Reheating with the expanded Simons Observatory
summary: The Simons Observatory will be extended by three Small Aperture Telescopes by 2027, increasing the total number of these instruments to six. We study the prospects for probing the reheating temperature and the inflaton coupling with this configuration, assuming a discovery of primordial gravitational waves in benchmark scenarios with a tensor-to-scalar ratio r=0.0036 or r=0.01. In popular plateau models of inflation, such an observation would fix the scale of inflation and enable determination of the order of magnitude of the reheating temperature and the inflaton interactions. For QCD-driven Warm Inflation the reheating temperature and inflaton coupling to gluons could, under optimistic assumptions, be measured with a precision of a few percent. Such a measurement would imply a clear prediction for complementary inflaton searches in axion experiments, paving the way toward probing the mechanism responsible for the initial conditions of the hot Big Bang in the laboratory.

AI.tldr: The Simons Observatory will expand to six Small Aperture Telescopes by 2027. This paper studies how detecting primordial gravitational waves (with tensor-to-scalar ratio r=0.0036 or r=0.01) could probe the reheating temperature and inflaton coupling. For plateau inflation models, this fixes the inflation scale and reveals the reheating temperature and inflaton interactions. For QCD-driven Warm Inflation, the inflaton coupling to gluons and reheating temperature could be measured with few percent precision, enabling complementary searches in axion experiments.
AI.motivation: To study the prospects for probing the reheating temperature and inflaton coupling using the upgraded Simons Observatory configuration, assuming a future detection of primordial gravitational waves.
AI.method: The study analyzes two benchmark scenarios with tensor-to-scalar ratios r=0.0036 and r=0.01, using popular plateau inflation models and QCD-driven Warm Inflation to forecast constraints on reheating parameters.
AI.result: For plateau inflation models, detecting primordial gravitational waves fixes the inflation scale and allows determination of the order of magnitude of the reheating temperature and inflaton interactions. For QCD-driven Warm Inflation, under optimistic assumptions, the reheating temperature and inflaton-gluon coupling could be measured with a few percent precision.
AI.conclusion: Such measurements would provide clear predictions for complementary inflaton searches in axion experiments, enabling laboratory probes of the mechanism responsible for the initial conditions of the hot Big Bang.

title: Dark and Luminous Matter in the Coma Cluster: Probing Galaxy Cluster Assembly Through Filaments with Weak Lensing and Multiwavelength Observations
summary: The Coma cluster (Abell 1656; $z=0.023$) is a nearby rich galaxy cluster and a key laboratory for studying cluster assembly in the Cosmic Web. We characterize its projected dark matter distribution and connection to galaxies, the intracluster medium, and reported intracluster filaments (ICFs) with wide-field ($\sim$12-deg$^2$) Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam weak-lensing (WL) analysis. We reconstruct the two-dimensional mass distribution, fit Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) models, derive an aperture mass densitometry profile, and compare the WL signal with optical spectroscopy, eROSITA X-ray observations, radio data, and gas fraction diagnostics. A single-halo NFW fit yields $M_{200\mathrm{c}}=8.2\pm0.7\times10^{14}~M_{\odot}$. The aperture mass profile agrees with the best-fit NFW model and the X-ray hydrostatic mass at $R\gtrsim20'$ ($\sim$560 kpc), suggesting little merger-induced bias in the global WL mass, while the inner region shows substantial hydrostatic bias. A two-halo NFW fit centered on NGC 4874 and NGC 4839 gives masses of $7.8\pm0.6$ and $0.9\pm0.2\times10^{14}~M_{\odot}$, implying a $\sim$1:8 minor merger. The gas mass fraction suggests that the system is returning from first apocenter. We find a positive spatial correlation between the WL signal and X-ray surface brightness, strongest along the ICF directions ($110^{\circ}$ and $340^{\circ}$), where shear-selected subhalos are predominantly detected. The Coma $r$-band mass-to-light ratio is radially constant with $\langle M/L_r\rangle\simeq250\pm66~M_{\odot}/L_{\odot}$ within $R_{200\mathrm{c}}$, whereas the northern and western ICFs show higher values of $\sim1000~M_{\odot}/L_{\odot}$, suggesting stronger dark matter dominance. These results show that joint WL and multiwavelength analyses can effectively probe cluster assembly and the dark matter content of ICFs.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam weak-lensing analysis to map the dark matter distribution of the Coma cluster, finding a single-halo mass of ~8.2×10¹⁴ M⊙, evidence of a 1:8 minor merger between NGC 4874 and NGC 4839, and radial constancy of the mass-to-light ratio (~250 M⊙/L⊙) within R₂₀₀c, while intracluster filaments show higher dark matter dominance (~1000 M⊙/L⊙).
AI.motivation: To characterize the projected dark matter distribution of the Coma cluster and its connection to galaxies, the intracluster medium, and reported intracluster filaments using wide-field weak-lensing analysis.
AI.method: Wide-field (~12 deg²) Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam weak-lensing analysis, including 2D mass reconstruction, NFW model fitting, aperture mass densitometry, and multiwavelength comparison with optical spectroscopy, eROSITA X-ray, radio data, and gas fraction diagnostics.
AI.result: Single-halo NFW fit yields M₂₀₀c = 8.2±0.7×10¹⁴ M⊙. Two-halo fit centered on NGC 4874 (7.8±0.6×10¹⁴ M⊙) and NGC 4839 (0.9±0.2×10¹⁴ M⊙) indicates a ~1:8 minor merger. Gas mass fraction suggests return from first apocenter. Positive spatial correlation between WL and X-ray brightness along ICF directions. Mass-to-light ratio is radially constant (~250 M⊙/L⊙) within R₂₀₀c, but ICFs show higher values (~1000 M⊙/L⊙).
AI.conclusion: Joint weak-lensing and multiwavelength analyses effectively probe cluster assembly and dark matter content of intracluster filaments.

title: Dark Matter with a Drag at Low Redshift
summary: Recent analyses of $fσ_8$ and weak-lensing data indicate that the linear growth rate at $z\lesssim 1$ may be lower than predicted by $Λ$CDM. This motivates models of dark matter in which large scale structure growth slows relative to $Λ$CDM at late times. We construct particle models in which dark matter experiences a drag with dark radiation that grows at late times, unlike conventional DM--DR interactions, which fade as the universe expands. A key ingredient is that the radiation interacting with the dark matter is produced at late times from dark matter decay. An explicit model, interacting Decaying Cold Dark Matter (iDCDM), adds two parameters beyond $Λ$CDM while leaving the background, BBN, and primary CMB intact. But it predicts a step-shaped suppression of the linear growth rate $f(k,z)$, a distinctive target for DESI, Euclid, and Rubin. Confronted with current data, iDCDM shows a modest preference over $Λ$CDM, driven by $fσ_8$, with $Δχ^2$ between $-2.7$ and $-7.6$ depending on the assumed scaling of the drag with redshift and on neutrino masses. The decisive test will come from upcoming $k$- and $z$-resolved growth measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a new dark matter model (iDCDM) where dark matter decays into dark radiation at late times, creating a drag that suppresses linear growth rate compared to ΛCDM, potentially explaining low-$z$ growth anomalies while preserving early universe physics.
AI.motivation: Recent $fσ_8$ and weak-lensing data suggest the linear growth rate at $z\lesssim 1$ may be lower than ΛCDM predictions, motivating dark matter models that slow structure growth at late times.
AI.method: Construct particle models where dark matter experiences a drag with dark radiation that grows at late times via dark matter decay into radiation. The explicit model, iDCDM, adds two parameters beyond ΛCDM and produces a step-shaped suppression of $f(k,z)$.
AI.result: iDCDM shows a modest preference over ΛCDM when confronted with current data, with $Δχ^2$ between $-2.7$ and $-7.6$ depending on drag redshift scaling and neutrino masses.
AI.conclusion: The distinctive step-shaped suppression of $f(k,z)$ is a target for DESI, Euclid, and Rubin; decisive tests require upcoming $k$- and $z$-resolved growth measurements.

title: Getting to know the Stellar Clusters in NGC 1569: Bayesian inference of stellar cluster properties in a dwarf starburst galaxy
summary: We present a Bayesian analysis of star clusters in the dwarf starburst galaxy NGC 1569 based on high-resolution Hubble Space Telescope imaging combined with integral-field spectroscopy from the Keck Cosmic Web Imager, obtained as part of the DUVET survey. For each cluster identified, we infer posterior probability distributions for mass and age using a forward modelling method that properly accounts for uncertainties due to stochastic sampling of the IMF. We investigate how the inferred properties depend on photometric coverage by repeating the analysis with different filter combinations, including mock extensions to the ultraviolet and near-infrared that emulate the addition of HST UV bands and James Webb Space Telescope imaging. We find that, while inclusion of these wavelength regimes further breaks age and mass degeneracies, the currently available data yields reasonably strong constraints on cluster parameters. We compare inferred cluster properties to the conditions of the local interstellar medium, and find evidence for multiple interesting correlations. The truncation mass of the cluster mass function varies with galactocentric distance, particularly moving off the disk, consistent with a dependence on the density of the interstellar medium. Cluster mass positively correlates with metallicity, suggesting that massive clusters preferentially form in pre-enriched gas, and the ionisation state of the gas, reflecting the increased prevalence of high-mass stars in high-mass clusters. These results demonstrate the power of Bayesian, initial mass function-aware modelling for resolving cluster populations in nearby starburst dwarfs and provide new insight into how cluster formation and feedback respond to local galactic conditions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a Bayesian analysis of star clusters in the dwarf starburst galaxy NGC 1569 using HST imaging and KCWI integral-field spectroscopy. By forward modeling with stochastic IMF sampling, the authors infer cluster mass and age posterior distributions, finding that current data provides strong constraints. They discover correlations between cluster properties and local ISM conditions: the cluster mass function truncation mass varies with galactocentric distance (correlated with ISM density), cluster mass positively correlates with metallicity, and massive clusters are associated with higher gas ionization states.
AI.motivation: To better understand how star cluster formation and feedback respond to local galactic conditions, particularly in nearby starburst dwarf galaxies, and to properly account for stochastic IMF sampling uncertainties when inferring cluster properties.
AI.method: Bayesian forward modeling with stochastic IMF sampling to infer posterior probability distributions for cluster mass and age; analysis repeated with different photometric filter combinations including mock UV and NIR extensions; comparison of inferred cluster properties to local ISM conditions.
AI.result: (1) Current HST+KCWI data yields strong constraints on cluster parameters despite degeneracies. (2) Cluster mass function truncation mass varies with galactocentric distance, consistent with ISM density dependence. (3) Cluster mass positively correlates with metallicity and gas ionization state.
AI.conclusion: Bayesian, IMF-aware modeling is a powerful tool for resolving cluster populations in starburst dwarfs, and cluster formation/feedback is tightly coupled to local galactic environment conditions.

title: Magnetic fields at the dawn of structure formation I. The CARLA J1510+5958 proto-cluster
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures, accepted for publication in A&A, shortened abstract to meet arXiv characters requirement
summary: Magnetic fields are a fundamental ingredient of the Universe, influencing the formation and evolution of cosmic structures. While magnetic fields in local galaxy clusters have been studied, their origin, amplification, and strength at high redshift are poorly understood. Proto-clusters represent the early stages of galaxy cluster formation, ideal for investigating the early magnetisation of the intra-cluster medium (ICM). We present a study of CARLA J1510+5958 proto-cluster at z = 1.72, observed with the JVLA in the L-band (1-2 GHz). We aim to investigate the magnetic field strength and structure in the proto-ICM and the role of AGN in magnetising the environment during early cluster formation. We analyse Faraday rotation on the polarised emission from the central radio-loud AGN using the Rotation Measure (RM) synthesis and QU fitting technique. We further interpret the observations with 3D simulations of gas density and turbulent magnetic fields, varying AGN orientation and path length. The two AGN lobes show different polarisation properties. The Western lobe exhibits a uniform RM (average $-115 \pm 32\text{ rad m}^{-2}$, dispersion $36 \pm 11\text{ rad m}^{-2}$), indicating a locally ordered magnetic field likely compressed by the lobe, while the Eastern lobe is depolarised. Although the asymmetry indicates a turbulent, magnetised medium, simulations rule out a purely isotropic random field for the Western lobe RM distribution. The QU fitting further suggests an internal Faraday component, interpreted as magnetised relativistic plasma from the lobe mixed with the surrounding gas, indicating possible magnetisation of the ambient medium by the AGN. From this asymmetry, we constrain the average physical magnetic field in the proto-ICM to a lower limit of 0.4 $μ$G. These results confirm a magnetised proto-ICM at z = 1.72, proving early field amplification during cluster assembly.

AI.tldr: Study of CARLA J1510+5958 proto-cluster at z=1.72 using JVLA L-band observations reveals magnetised proto-ICM with lower limit of 0.4 μG field strength, showing asymmetric AGN lobe polarisation that indicates early magnetic field amplification during cluster formation.
AI.motivation: Magnetic fields in high-redshift proto-clusters are poorly understood; this work aims to investigate the early magnetisation of the intra-cluster medium (ICM) during the formation epoch of galaxy clusters.
AI.method: Faraday rotation analysis (RM synthesis and QU fitting) on polarised emission from a central radio-loud AGN in the CARLA J1510+5958 proto-cluster, combined with 3D simulations of gas density and turbulent magnetic fields varying AGN orientation and path length.
AI.result: Western lobe shows uniform RM (-115±32 rad/m², dispersion 36±11 rad/m²) indicating ordered compressed magnetic field; Eastern lobe is depolarised. Asymmetry rules out purely isotropic random field. Internal Faraday component detected suggesting AGN-driven magnetisation of ambient medium. Lower limit of 0.4 μG for proto-ICM magnetic field.
AI.conclusion: Proto-ICM at z=1.72 is already magnetised, confirming early magnetic field amplification during cluster assembly, with AGN playing a role in magnetising the environment.

title: DESI as sparse Integral Field Spectrograph I: Spatially resolved chemical enrichment in star-forming galaxies at $z\leq0.1$
comment: Submitted to The Astrophysical Journal; comments are welcome
summary: We present a spatially resolved chemical abundance analysis of 2291 star-forming galaxies at $z \leq 0.1$, spanning nearly four orders of magnitude in stellar mass ($8 \le \rm log (M_{\star}/M_{\odot}) \le 11.5$), by exploiting the multi-fibre spectra from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) as a sparse integral field spectrograph. In the inner regions ($<2R_e$), the radial gas-phase metallicity profiles show an outward-declining trend for massive galaxies, with the steepest gradient ($\nabla_{log(O/H)}$) $\sim-0.08$ dex/R$_{e}$, whereas low-mass dwarf galaxies exhibit nearly flat profiles ($\nabla_{log(O/H)}\sim-0.02$ dex/R$_{e}$). The large galactocentric radii ($\sim$5 R$_{e}$) probed in this study, reveal flat metallicity profiles near the disk-halo interface. Strikingly, these flat metallicity values are consistent across a wide stellar mass range, likely reflecting the influence of low SFR and metal poor inflows in the outer regions. The metallicity gradient - stellar mass relation exhibits a turnover at $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.5$, beyond which gradients become shallower, possibly driven by the chemical equilibrium in the inner disk of massive galaxies and/or dilution from cosmic gas accretion. At fixed stellar mass, a strong size dependence is observed, where compact galaxies show flatter gradients and higher central enrichment than their extended counterparts. The abundance gradients are further linked with the stellar age distribution within the galactic disk, where galaxies with younger outskirts show steeper gradients than the ones with older outskirts, consistent with ongoing inside-out disc growth sustaining centrally concentrated chemical enrichment. These results underscore the interplay of star formation efficiency, stellar feedback, and metal-poor gas accretion in governing the radial chemical structure in galaxies.

AI.tldr: Analysis of spatially resolved gas-phase metallicity profiles for 2291 low-redshift star-forming galaxies using DESI, revealing mass-dependent gradients, flat outer profiles, a gradient-mass turnover at ~10.5 M☉, size-dependent central enrichment, and links to stellar age distribution supporting inside-out disk growth.
AI.motivation: To understand the radial chemical structure of galaxies across a wide stellar mass range and its connection to star formation, feedback, and gas accretion processes.
AI.method: Spatially resolved chemical abundance analysis of 2291 star-forming galaxies at z≤0.1 using DESI multi-fibre spectra as a sparse integral field spectrograph, covering 8 ≤ log(M*/M⊙) ≤ 11.5.
AI.result: Massive galaxies show steep outward-declining metallicity gradients (~−0.08 dex/Re), while low-mass dwarfs show flat profiles (~−0.02 dex/Re). Flat metallicity profiles at ~5 Re are consistent across stellar mass. A gradient-mass turnover occurs at log(M*/M⊙)~10.5. Compact galaxies have flatter gradients and higher central enrichment. Galaxies with younger outskirts show steeper gradients.
AI.conclusion: The radial chemical structure in galaxies is governed by the interplay of star formation efficiency, stellar feedback, and metal-poor gas accretion, with evidence for inside-out disk growth.

title: Complex yet Hermitian: Gaussian covariance of cross-correlation and multi-tracer power spectra
summary: Accurate modelling of the covariance of clustering observables is essential to fully exploit current and future survey data, which is expected to constrain large-scale clustering signals with unprecedented precision. Computational costs of simulation-based estimates motivate analytical approaches, especially in light of the growing interest towards multi-tracer analyses and parity-odd signatures in two-point statistics, which respectively mitigate cosmic variance and probe relativistic projection effects on cosmological scales. In this work, we generalise previous theoretical results for the Gaussian covariance of multi-tracer power spectrum measurements, providing a general expression applicable to both real (even-parity) and complex (both even- and odd-parity) power spectra. We focus on a generic weighted estimator at first, and then showcase how our general formalism applies to Legendre power spectrum multipoles and two-dimensional power spectrum, recovering known limits in appropriate cases. We validate our predictions against Gaussian Monte Carlo simulations and investigate the structure of the covariance matrix, including the Hermitian properties of its imaginary part.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes theoretical results for Gaussian covariance of multi-tracer power spectrum measurements, providing expressions applicable to both real (even-parity) and complex (both even- and odd-parity) power spectra, validated against Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.motivation: Accurate covariance modeling of clustering observables is essential for exploiting current and future survey data with unprecedented precision, particularly for multi-tracer analyses and parity-odd signatures that mitigate cosmic variance and probe relativistic projection effects.
AI.method: The authors derive a general expression for Gaussian covariance of multi-tracer power spectra applicable to both real and complex spectra. They first focus on a generic weighted estimator, then apply the formalism to Legendre power spectrum multipoles and the 2D power spectrum, recovering known limits. Validation is performed against Gaussian Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.result: The general covariance formalism is validated against simulations. The structure of the covariance matrix is investigated, including the Hermitian properties of its imaginary part.
AI.conclusion: The generalized framework provides an analytical approach to covariance estimation for multi-tracer analyses, supporting both even- and odd-parity power spectra, which is computationally efficient compared to simulation-based estimates.

title: Constraining the Geometry of Galactic Dark Matter with Gaia Data Release 3
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We derive both the mid-plane and off-plane rotation curves, $v_c(R,z)$, and the vertical acceleration, $a_z(R,z)$, of the Milky Way (MW) using \textit{Gaia}~DR3 data over the ranges of vertical heights $z \in (-2,2)\,$ kpc and galactocentric distances $R \in (8.5,14)$ kpc where the velocity components are determined with high precision, i.e., with an error $< 5\%$. In contrast, the vertical acceleration $a_z(R,z)$ is dominated by model-dependent systematics, with uncertainties of up to $\sim 20\%$. This level of accuracy allows us to place stringent constraints on the geometry of the MW's dark matter (DM) distribution, as the vertical gradients of the gravitational potential attain their maximum within this range of radial and vertical distances corresponding to the characteristic scales of the disk. We find that models including the observed stellar components together with a spherical DM halo fail to reproduce both the pronounced variation of $v_c(R,z)$ with height and the observed behavior of $a_z(R,z)$. In particular, spherical halos with a scale radius of $r_s \sim 15$ kpc contribute negligibly to the off-plane rotation curve and vertical acceleration in the inner disk, leaving these features primarily determined by the stellar mass distribution. Conversely, models in which DM is confined to a flattened, disk-like configuration predict substantial contributions to both $v_c(R,z)$ and $a_z(R,z)$, resulting in a markedly better agreement with the data. We conclude that disk-like DM distributions are strongly favored over spherical halo models. Forthcoming Gaia data releases will enable even more stringent tests of the geometry and distribution of the MW's DM component.

AI.tldr: Using Gaia DR3 data, the authors derive Milky Way rotation curves and vertical acceleration, finding that spherical dark matter halo models fail to match observations, while flattened, disk-like dark matter distributions are strongly favored.
AI.motivation: To constrain the geometry of the Milky Way's dark matter distribution by analyzing mid-plane and off-plane rotation curves and vertical acceleration derived from high-precision Gaia DR3 data.
AI.method: Derived v_c(R,z) and a_z(R,z) from Gaia DR3 over R ∈ (8.5,14) kpc and z ∈ (-2,2) kpc, with velocity errors < 5%. Compared observed features to models with spherical DM halos vs. flattened disk-like DM distributions.
AI.result: Spherical halo models (r_s ~ 15 kpc) fail to reproduce the height variation of v_c(R,z) and observed a_z(R,z); disk-like DM distributions yield substantially better agreement with data.
AI.conclusion: Disk-like (flattened) DM distributions are strongly favored over spherical halo models for the Milky Way's inner disk region.

title: Galaxy formation in modified gravity -- II. galaxy halo connection and assembly bias
summary: Modern surveys such as DESI and \textit{Euclid}, which collect data for hundreds of millions of galaxies to map the large-scale structure (LSS) of the Universe, hold the key to determining the cosmological parameters and testing new physics. This ambition, however, is limited by uncertainties in the galaxy-halo connection: the link between observed galaxies and the underlying, unobservable matter field, by accounting for effects such as galaxy bias and assembly bias (AB). These are particularly poorly-understood for modified gravity (MG) models, which are popular alternatives to the cosmological constant to explain accelerated expansion. We approach this problem using mock emission line galaxy (ELG) and luminous red galaxy (LRG) catalogues in $f(R)$ gravity matching the specifications of ongoing Stage-IV galaxy surveys, generated from state-of-the-art MG hydrodynamical simulations. While the interplay between MG -- especially the chameleon screening mechanism -- and galaxy formation leaves complicated imprints in the galaxy-halo connection, a simple physical picture emerges in which halo and galaxy formation are enhanced for progressively more massive haloes over time. We confirm that the basic galaxy-halo connection model, the halo occupation distribution (HOD), in which galaxy occupation is determined solely by halo mass, underestimates galaxy clustering strength in $Λ$CDM by $10$--$20\%$ at $z\lesssim1$ when neglecting AB, and demonstrate that MG introduces further complexity. Extending this model with a suitably-chosen environment density as a secondary HOD variable reduces the AB effect in all models to $2$--$3\%$ for $z\lesssim0.5$. This provides a well-motivated starting point for further works on minimising the impact of AB when testing non-standard cosmological models with LSS.

AI.tldr: Mock ELG and LRG catalogues in f(R) gravity from MG hydrodynamical simulations show that the galaxy-halo connection is affected by modified gravity and assembly bias; extending HOD with environment density reduces AB effects to 2-3% at z<0.5.
AI.motivation: To accurately determine cosmological parameters and test new physics using Stage-IV galaxy surveys like DESI and Euclid, the uncertainties in the galaxy-halo connection—particularly galaxy bias and assembly bias—must be understood, especially for modified gravity models where these effects are poorly known.
AI.method: Mock emission line galaxy (ELG) and luminous red galaxy (LRG) catalogues in f(R) gravity were generated from state-of-the-art MG hydrodynamical simulations, matching Stage-IV survey specifications. The standard halo occupation distribution (HOD) model and an extended version with environment density as a secondary variable were compared.
AI.result: The standard HOD underestimates ΛCDM clustering by 10-20% at z<1 when neglecting assembly bias; MG introduces further complexity. Extending HOD with environment density reduces AB effects to 2-3% for z<0.5 across all models.
AI.conclusion: A simple physical picture emerges where halo/galaxy formation is enhanced in more massive haloes over time under MG with chameleon screening. The environment-extended HOD provides a well-motivated starting point for minimizing AB impact when testing non-standard cosmological models with LSS.

title: CAPOS: The bulge Cluster APOgee Survey XII. Abundances for 98 PIGS metal-poor Bulge field giants
summary: The inner Milky Way hosts overlapping stellar populations (bar--bulge, inner thin and thick disks, and halo), complicating population assignments along the line of sight. A joint chemical--dynamical approach is required to isolate a clean field bulge sample. Metal-poor bulge stars are valuable as they likely trace the earliest phases of chemical enrichment in the inner Galaxy. We aim to characterize the alpha-element (Si, Mg) and selected Fe-peak abundances of a dynamically defined sample of bulge field stars, and to contrast these trends with the inner-halo tail in the metal-poor regime. We analyze metal-poor candidates from the Pristine Inner Galaxy Survey observed by the bulge Cluster APOGEE Survey. Using APOGEE/ASPCAP abundances (S/N >= 50), we integrate full 6D orbits in a barred Milky Way potential. Bulge membership is defined via orbital confinement using an apocenter cut and the high-density locus in the (E_J, L_z) plane, with uncertainties estimated using Monte Carlo simulations. We identify 98 stars as bulge members. The metallicity distribution spans -2.5 <= [Fe/H] <= -0.4, with a median [Fe/H] = -1.71, offset to higher metallicity than the inner halo (median [Fe/H] = -1.96). The sample follows a high-alpha sequence with slopes d[Si/Fe]/d[Fe/H] = -0.020(+0.012,-0.051) and d[Mg/Fe]/d[Fe/H] = -0.097(+0.062,-0.133). Fe-peak tracers show [Ni/Fe] ~ 0, while [Mn/Fe] declines with [Fe/H] with a mild upturn at higher metallicity. We detect no significant [Si/Fe] gradients with R_apo or Z_max (+0.010(+0.018,0.000) and +0.006(+0.022,-0.011) dex kpc^-1, respectively). Results are insensitive to Omega_p, yielding indistinguishable memberships. The chemo-orbital evidence favors an in situ origin within the inner Galaxy for the metal-poor bulge field, enriched at early times and rearranged by secular bar evolution, with a minor contribution from halo stars at the most metal-poor end.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a joint chemical-dynamical approach to isolate 98 metal-poor bulge field stars from the Pristine Inner Galaxy Survey + APOGEE, finding they span -2.5 ≤ [Fe/H] ≤ -0.4, follow a high-alpha sequence, show no radial or vertical alpha-abundance gradients, and are consistent with in situ origin enriched early and reshuffled by secular bar evolution, with minor halo contamination at the lowest metallicities.
AI.motivation: The inner Milky Way contains overlapping stellar populations (bar-bulge, inner disks, halo), making population assignments difficult. A joint chemical-dynamical approach is needed to isolate a clean field bulge sample. Metal-poor bulge stars are valuable because they likely trace the earliest phases of chemical enrichment in the inner Galaxy.
AI.method: Metal-poor candidates from the Pristine Inner Galaxy Survey observed by APOGEE were analyzed. Using APOGEE/ASPCAP abundances (S/N ≥ 50), full 6D orbits were integrated in a barred Milky Way potential. Bulge membership was defined via orbital confinement using an apocenter cut and the high-density locus in the (E_J, L_z) plane, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.result: 98 bulge members identified, metallicity spanning -2.5 ≤ [Fe/H] ≤ -0.4 (median -1.71). Sample follows high-alpha sequence: d[Si/Fe]/d[Fe/H] = -0.020 and d[Mg/Fe]/d[Fe/H] = -0.097. [Ni/Fe] ~ 0; [Mn/Fe] declines with [Fe/H] with mild upturn at higher metallicity. No significant [Si/Fe] gradients with R_apo or Z_max. Results insensitive to Omega_p.
AI.conclusion: Chemo-orbital evidence favors an in situ origin within the inner Galaxy for the metal-poor bulge field, enriched at early times and rearranged by secular bar evolution, with a minor contribution from halo stars at the most metal-poor end.

title: Weak Lensing Spectrotomography: A1767 and A2065
comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables, accepted for publication in the Journal of the Korean Astronomical Society
summary: We describe spectroscopic tomographic weak lensing measurements (spectrotomography) for two rich clusters of galaxies, A1767 and A2065, based on extensive spectroscopy and Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) imaging. These detections represent the first use of spectrotomography based on archival Subaru/HSC imaging. The measurements depend only on galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts reported here. The approach cleanly separates cluster members from the background and suppresses systematics that may be introduced by the use of photometric background redshifts. We detect the tomographic shear signals at $3.1σ$ (A1767) and $3.5σ$ (A2065). The shear signal amplitudes are consistent with the cluster dynamical (caustic) masses and they scale appropriately with source redshift. However, comparison with the first spectrophotometric detection of A2029 based on DECam imaging reveals some subtle potential systematic issues in deriving the shear signal for the relatively bright background galaxies used in the analysis. These issues may be important for understanding future more extensive applications of spectrotomography based on further Subaru imaging, as well as Euclid and LSST data. The total of three spectrophotometric detections (A1767, A2029, and A2065) sets the stage for broader application of the technique for unbiased cluster weak lensing mass determinations and potentially for a geometric cosmological test that is independent of other methods.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the first spectroscopic tomographic weak lensing measurements (spectrotomography) for two galaxy clusters, A1767 and A2065, using Subaru/HSC imaging and archival spectroscopy, achieving 3.1σ and 3.5σ shear detections. The method isolates cluster members from background galaxies using spectroscopic redshifts, avoiding photometric redshift systematics. While mass estimates are consistent with dynamical (caustic) masses, comparison with A2029 reveals subtle systematic issues for bright background galaxies. These results pave the way for unbiased cluster mass measurements and a geometric cosmological test.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate spectrotomography — weak lensing using only spectroscopic redshifts — as a clean method that avoids photometric redshift systematics, enabling unbiased cluster mass determinations and a geometric cosmological test independent of other methods.
AI.method: Spectroscopic tomographic weak lensing (spectrotomography) applied to two clusters (A1767 and A2065) using Subaru/HSC imaging and archival spectroscopy. The analysis uses only galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts, cleanly separating cluster members from background sources. Shear signals are measured as a function of source redshift (tomography), and results are compared to cluster dynamical (caustic) masses and to a previous spectrophotometric detection of A2029 (DECam).
AI.result: Shear signals detected at 3.1σ (A1767) and 3.5σ (A2065). Amplitudes consistent with dynamical/caustic masses and scale with source redshift. However, comparison with A2029 reveals subtle systematic issues for bright background galaxies used in the analysis.
AI.conclusion: Three spectrophotometric detections (A1767, A2029, A2065) set the stage for broader application of spectrotomography for unbiased cluster weak lensing mass determinations and a geometric cosmological test independent of other methods. The identified systematic issues with bright background galaxies must be addressed for future applications with Subaru imaging, Euclid, and LSST.

title: Influence of the resonance ring gravity on the stellar velocity distribution near the OLR of the Galactic bar
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in Astrophysical Bulletin
summary: We constructed the 2D model of the Galaxy which initially includes an analytical bar, bulge, disk and halo. The model disk forms the outer elliptical resonance rings R1 and R2 located near the outer Lindblad resonance of the bar (OLR), as well as the inner resonance ring r located near the corotation radius (CR). As the density of stars in the elliptical rings increased, we introduced additional gravitational perturbations created by the rings. The radial component of gravitational perturbations from the elliptical rings, F_R, at a point with the Galactocentric coordinates (R, theta) was represented as a combination of three polynomials in powers R/Re or Re/R, where Re is the distance to the midline (middle) of the ring at a given angle theta. The azimuthal component of the disturbances, F_T, was calculated using the force F_R. The difference between the values of the force F_R (F_T) calculated using the numerical differentiation of the potential and using the analytical representation does not exceed 5.7% (1.3%) of the maximum value of the force F_R generated by the elliptical rings. In general, the gravity of the elliptical rings has little effect on the process of adjustment of epicyclic motions near the OLR of the bar.

AI.tldr: A 2D Galactic model with analytical bar, bulge, disk, halo, and elliptical resonance rings (R1, R2 near OLR, r near CR) is constructed. An analytical representation of ring gravitational perturbations (polynomials in R/Re or Re/R) achieves high accuracy (<5.7% radial, <1.3% azimuthal force error) but shows minimal impact on epicyclic adjustment near OLR.
AI.motivation: To construct a realistic 2D Galactic model including resonance rings and develop an accurate analytical representation of their gravitational perturbations.
AI.method: A 2D model with analytical bar, bulge, disk, and halo. Outer elliptical rings R1/R2 at OLR and inner ring r at CR formed naturally. Additional ring perturbations were represented as polynomials in R/Re or Re/R; azimuthal component derived from radial component.
AI.result: Radial force deviation ≤5.7%, azimuthal force deviation ≤1.3% of max radial force from rings, compared to numerical differentiation. Ring gravity has little effect on epicyclic adjustment near OLR.
AI.conclusion: The analytical representation of ring gravitational perturbations is accurate, but ring self-gravity does not significantly alter the dynamics near the bar's outer Lindblad resonance.

title: Identification of Lensed Gravitational-Wave Beat Patterns by LISA
summary: Strong lensing of massive black hole binaries can produce multiple gravitational-wave images with different magnifications and arrival times. LISA signals remain in band for months to years, allowing multiple lensed images to overlap during the inspiral stage and generate beat patterns. A singular isothermal sphere lens model is adopted to describe the lensing configuration, and two-image beat waveforms are constructed from massive black hole binary signals. To isolate the beat pattern itself, waveform mismatch is evaluated only during the overlapping inspiral stage before the coalescence of the first image, excluding contributions from the delayed merger peak of the second image. Using the HS-nod-SN (B+20) strong-lensing population, the occurrence rate of identifiable beat events is estimated, and Bayesian parameter estimation is performed with a beat template. Beat patterns are most readily identified when the lensing time delay is short and the delayed image has a relatively large magnification. Among 196 detectable two-image lensed events, 92 satisfy the temporal-overlap condition and 14 satisfy the beat-identification criterion, corresponding to an identifiable beat fraction of about 7\%. Posterior inference shows that the beat template can recover the lensing time delay and magnification parameters for a representative beat event. These results indicate that lensed beat patterns constitute a distinguishable subset of strongly lensed LISA events and provide a unique observational signature of strong lensing in the LISA band.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes gravitational-wave beat patterns from strongly lensed massive black hole binaries in the LISA band, finding that ~7% of detectable lensed events produce identifiable beats when lensing time delays are short and magnifications are large, with Bayesian inference successfully recovering lensing parameters.
AI.motivation: Strong lensing of massive black hole binaries can produce multiple gravitational-wave images with overlapping signals that generate unique beat patterns, providing a distinct observational signature of strong lensing in the LISA frequency band.
AI.method: Use a singular isothermal sphere lens model to describe lensing configuration; construct two-image beat waveforms from massive black hole binary signals; evaluate waveform mismatch during overlapping inspiral stage; use HS-nod-SN (B+20) population for occurrence rate estimation; perform Bayesian parameter estimation with a beat template.
AI.result: Among 196 detectable two-image lensed events, 92 satisfy temporal overlap and 14 satisfy beat identification (≈7% identifiable beat fraction). Beat patterns are most identifiable when lensing time delay is short and the delayed image has large magnification.
AI.conclusion: Lensed beat patterns constitute a distinguishable subset of strongly lensed LISA events and provide a unique observational signature of strong lensing in the LISA band.

title: Feedback-Free Star Formation in Clusters within a Galaxy Simulated at High Resolution in Cosmic Dawn
comment: 15 pages, 17 figures. Submitted to MNRAS. All comments are welcome
summary: We perform a cosmological zoom-in simulation of a massive galaxy ($M_s\sim10^{10}\rm M_\odot$ at $z\sim10$) using the GIZMO code. By employing $\leq 3\rm pc$ resolution and a $3.4\rm Myr$ supernova feedback delay, we capture the feedback-free starbursts (FFB) in clusters. The simulation reproduces FFB model predictions and super-bright galaxies observed by JWST. At $z\sim10$, cold streams feed a compact galaxy ($R_{\rm e}\sim1\rm kpc$), with stellar and surface densities ($>10^5\rm cm^{-3}$, $>10^5\rm M_\odot pc^{-2}$) exceeding FFB thresholds. The global star-formation efficiency (SFE) is $\varepsilon_s\sim0.2\text{--}0.3$, associated with a fluctuating star-formation history. We identified over $10^5$ star clusters ($M_{\star}>10^{4.5}\rm M_\odot$) with a nearly scale-free mass distribution (${\rm d}N/{{\rm d}\log M}\propto M^{-1.06}$). Approximately 90\% of star formation occurs in clusters, which at a given time constitute $30\text{--}40\%$ of the total stellar mass. The star formation in most of the clusters of masses $<10^7\rm M_\odot$, occurs in bursts of $<3\rm Myr$ and a local SFE $\sim0.5\pm 0.2$. Cluster metallicities ($-2.01<\log (Z/Z_\odot)<-0.45$) indicate rapid baryon recycling. Feedback-driven outflows exhibit typical temperature of $10^7\rm K$ and typical velocities of $\sim 2000\rm km\ s^{-1}$. In the highly dynamic central $1\rm kpc$, clusters undergo rapid orbital decay and merge to assemble the oblate nuclear stellar cluster. Cluster shapes range from oblate to prolate, with a triaxial median. These clusters are consistent with JWST observations, and a fraction of them may survive to yield the globular clusters (GCs) at low redshifts.

AI.tldr: A cosmological zoom-in simulation of a massive galaxy at z~10 using GIZMO with ≤3 pc resolution and 3.4 Myr supernova feedback delay reproduces feedback-free starbursts (FFB) and JWST-observed super-bright galaxies. The galaxy is compact (Re~1 kpc), with high stellar/surface densities exceeding FFB thresholds. Global SFE is 0.2–0.3. Over 10^5 star clusters form with a near scale-free mass distribution (dN/dlogM ∝ M^-1.06). ~90% of star formation occurs in clusters, most <10^7 M⊙ in bursts <3 Myr with local SFE ~0.5. Cluster metallicities indicate rapid baryon recycling. Feedback-driven outflows reach ~10^7 K and ~2000 km/s. Clusters undergo rapid orbital decay and merging, forming an oblate nuclear stellar cluster. Shapes range oblate to prolate, triaxial median. Some clusters may survive to become globular clusters at low redshifts.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation of massive galaxies at high redshift (z~10) and test the feedback-free starburst (FFB) model as an explanation for the unexpectedly bright galaxies observed by JWST.
AI.method: Cosmological zoom-in simulation using the GIZMO code with ≤3 pc spatial resolution and a 3.4 Myr delay for supernova feedback, enabling resolved star cluster formation and feedback-free starbursts.
AI.result: Simulation reproduces FFB model predictions and JWST-observed super-bright galaxies. Over 10^5 star clusters form with scale-free mass distribution; ~90% of star formation occurs in clusters; most clusters <10^7 M⊙ burst in <3 Myr with local SFE ~0.5; outflows reach 10^7 K and ~2000 km/s; clusters merge to form an oblate nuclear stellar cluster.
AI.conclusion: The FFB mechanism can successfully explain the existence of super-bright high-z galaxies observed by JWST. The simulated star cluster population is consistent with JWST observations and a fraction may survive to become present-day globular clusters.

title: Geometric obstruction to resolving the Hubble tension: orthogonality of scale and shape in distance measurements
summary: We identify a geometric obstruction to resolving the Hubble tension by combining early-time sound-horizon reduction with late-time smooth dark energy. Within $Λ$CDM, the BAO--SN matter-density gap $ΔΩ_m = 0.037$ is exactly invariant under the sound-horizon rescaling $α\equiv r_s^{\rm mod}/r_s^{Λ{\rm CDM}}$, and late-time $w(z)$ deformations cannot eliminate this gap either: reconciling the two datasets requires \emph{opposite} deformations -- phantom ($w < -1$) for BAO, quintessence ($w > -1$) for SN at $z < 0.5$ -- an anti-alignment quantified by $\cosθ= -0.97$ in $w(z)$ space. A full MCMC analysis of DESI DR2 BAO, Planck plik\_lite, and Pantheon+ bears this out: the optimal $α^* = 0.992$ ($0.8\%$ $r_s$ reduction) brings the joint fit to $H_0 = 70.3 \pm 0.3\;\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, still $3.2σ$ below SH0ES, with the inter-dataset tension reduced but not removed. The obstruction reflects not a shortage of model freedom but an irreducible disagreement between probes. The deformation space $\{α, β_{\rm damp}, w(z)\}$ already spans $93\%$ of the $Ω_m$ response direction; nonetheless BAO and SN constrain $Ω_m$ through independent channels and disagree, while the residual $H_0$ deficit, anchored by the local distance ladder, resides in the absolute distance scale that $w(z)$ reshapes but cannot rescale.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies a geometric obstruction to resolving the Hubble tension via early-time sound-horizon reduction combined with late-time dark energy. Within ΛCDM, the BAO–SN matter-density gap ΔΩₘ = 0.037 is invariant under sound-horizon rescaling, and late-time w(z) deformations cannot eliminate it because BAO and SN require opposite deformations (phantom vs. quintessence). A full MCMC analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, Planck plik_lite, and Pantheon+ yields optimal α* = 0.992 (0.8% r_s reduction) and H₀ = 70.3 ± 0.3 km/s/Mpc, still 3.2σ below SH0ES. The obstruction reflects irreducible disagreement between probes rather than insufficient model freedom.
AI.motivation: To test whether combining early-time sound-horizon reduction with late-time smooth dark energy can resolve the Hubble tension, and to identify fundamental geometric obstructions from BAO and SN data.
AI.method: Analytical geometric analysis of parameter-space degeneracies, combined with full MCMC analysis using DESI DR2 BAO, Planck plik_lite, and Pantheon+ supernova data, exploring deformation space {α, β_damp, w(z)}.
AI.result: The BAO–SN matter-density gap ΔΩₘ = 0.037 is invariant under r_s rescaling α. Late-time w(z) deformations require opposite signs for BAO (phantom, w < -1) and SN (quintessence, w > -1) at z < 0.5, with cosθ = -0.97 anti-alignment. The optimal fit yields H₀ = 70.3 ± 0.3 km/s/Mpc, still 3.2σ below SH0ES. The deformation space spans 93% of the Ωₘ response direction, yet tension persists.
AI.conclusion: The Hubble tension cannot be resolved by combining early-time r_s reduction with late-time smooth dark energy because BAO and SN data have an irreducible disagreement in Ωₘ constraints that is geometrically protected. The residual H₀ deficit is anchored in the absolute distance scale that w(z) can reshape but not rescale.

title: Carbon Abundances in Metal-Poor Stars Reveal Distinct Galaxy and Star Formation Pathways in the Early Universe
summary: Carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP; with $\rm{[Fe/H]} \le -2.0$ and $\rm{[C/Fe]} \ge 0.7$) stars preserve information about early chemical enrichment, low-mass star formation, and the hierarchical assembly of galaxies. In this study, we have compiled an extensive literature sample of 1032 stellar carbon abundances spanning the metal-poor Milky Way halo (437 stars), 21 ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs; 102 stars), seven classical dwarf spheroidal galaxies (254 stars), three accreted dwarf galaxies (90 stars), the Small Accreted Stellar Systems (SASS; 77 stars), and eleven stellar streams (72 stars). We establish the fractions of CEMP stars for each of these systems and categories. Generally, the low-mass UFDs possess the high fractions at low metallicities, whereas the more massive classical dwarf galaxies have relatively few CEMP stars. This behavior reveals a new low-metallicity Magnitude ($M_{\rm V}$)--CEMP Fraction relation across the dwarf satellite galaxy population. The high CEMP fractions in surviving UFDs suggest their enrichment was dominated by faint supernovae, as higher energy input would likely have quenched star production. The low CEMP fractions in classical dwarfs imply predominantly in situ formation rather than assembly from smaller systems. Using $\rm{[C/H]}$ abundances, we also probe early low-mass star formation. Eight stars lie within or near the theoretical ''forbidden zone'', indicating that dust-induced cooling, alongside fine-structure line cooling, contributed to early star formation. These rare dust-cooled stars may have formed in UFD-like systems that did not survive. Overall, the metal-poor Milky Way halo appears to have assembled from many different dwarf galaxies, with CEMP halo stars being contributed by early UFD-like systems and non-CEMP halo stars by intermediate-sized halos that later formed classical dwarfs.

AI.tldr: This study compiles 1032 carbon abundances across various Milky Way satellite systems to establish CEMP star fractions, revealing a new MV–CEMP fraction relation where low-mass UFDs have high CEMP fractions (dominated by faint supernovae) and classical dwarfs have low CEMP fractions (implying in-situ formation), with eight stars in the "forbidden zone" indicating dust-induced cooling contributed to early star formation.
AI.motivation: To understand early chemical enrichment, low-mass star formation, and hierarchical galaxy assembly by analyzing carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP) stars across different Milky Way satellite systems and relating their fractions to system properties.
AI.method: Compiled a literature sample of 1032 stellar carbon abundances from the Milky Way halo, 21 UFDs, 7 classical dwarf spheroidals, 3 accreted dwarfs, SASS, and 11 stellar streams, then computed CEMP fractions per system.
AI.result: Low-mass UFDs have high CEMP fractions at low metallicities; classical dwarfs have few CEMP stars; a new MV–CEMP Fraction relation is found; eight stars lie in the theoretical "forbidden zone"; CEMP halo stars came from UFD-like systems, non-CEMP from intermediate-sized halos.
AI.conclusion: High CEMP fractions in UFDs indicate enrichment by faint supernovae; low fractions in classical dwarfs suggest in-situ formation; dust-induced cooling contributed to early star formation; the Milky Way halo assembled from diverse dwarf galaxy progenitors.

title: Cluster Mass Inference from Galaxy Kinematics
summary: The masses of galaxy clusters carry cosmological and astrophysical information. We develop a simulation-based inference pipeline to infer cluster masses from full projected phase-space information of member and interloper galaxies. Our method combines a permutation-invariant Deep Sets architecture with neural posterior estimation using normalizing flows, enabling the recovery of expressive posterior distributions. We train the model to predict residual corrections to the classical $M$--$σ$ relation, thus explicitly isolating information beyond velocity dispersion. Using the Uchuu-UniverseMachine simulation, we evaluate the method under both idealized (interloper-free) and realistic (cylindrical) observational setups. In the idealized case, our model reduces the scatter in mass estimates to as low as $\sim 0.1$ dex, representing a twofold improvement over the traditional $M$--$σ$ relation. In the cylindrical setup, we achieve comparable performance at the high-mass end ($> 10^{14.5}\,M_\odot/h$), demonstrating robustness against interloper contamination. We demonstrate that set-based simulation-driven inference provides a powerful and flexible framework for galaxy cluster mass estimation, enabling improved accuracy and reliable uncertainty characterization for upcoming large-scale surveys. Our model saturates the kinematic information content and thus suggests a baseline for future studies.

AI.tldr: A simulation-based inference pipeline using Deep Sets and normalizing flows infers galaxy cluster masses from full projected phase-space information, achieving ~0.1 dex scatter (twofold improvement over M-σ relation) and robustness to interloper contamination.
AI.motivation: Galaxy cluster masses carry cosmological and astrophysical information, but traditional mass estimators (e.g., M-σ relation) are limited by scatter and sensitivity to interlopers. More accurate and robust mass inference is needed for upcoming large-scale surveys.
AI.method: A permutation-invariant Deep Sets architecture combined with neural posterior estimation via normalizing flows is trained on the Uchuu-UniverseMachine simulation to predict residual corrections to the classical M-σ relation, using full projected phase-space information of member and interloper galaxies under both idealized (interloper-free) and realistic (cylindrical) observational setups.
AI.result: In the idealized case, scatter reduces to ~0.1 dex (twofold improvement over M-σ). In the cylindrical setup, comparable performance is achieved at high masses (>10^14.5 M⊙/h), demonstrating robustness to interloper contamination. The model saturates the kinematic information content.
AI.conclusion: Set-based simulation-driven inference provides a powerful and flexible framework for galaxy cluster mass estimation, improving accuracy and enabling reliable uncertainty characterization for large-scale surveys, and establishes a baseline for future studies.

title: The X-ray photon index Eddington ratio relation in radio-quiet quasars from XMM-Newton and SDSS
summary: This study presents a comprehensive X-ray spectroscopic analysis of 642 quasars, obtained by cross-matching the XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalog (DR11) with the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (DR16) quasar catalog. After stringent quality filtering and automated spectral reduction, we derived reliable photon indices ($Γ$) and intrinsic 2--10 keV X-ray luminosities. Using multiwavelength data, sources were classified into 561 radio-quiet (RQ) and 81 radio-loud (RL) quasars. We estimate the bolometric luminosity and Eddington ratio ($λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$) from absorption-corrected X-ray measurements and virial black hole masses. Our primary objective is to establish and characterize the fundamental relationship between the photon index and Eddington ratio for RQ population. We find that RQ quasars exhibit systematically higher Eddington ratios, peaking at $\log λ_{\mathrm{Edd}} \approx -1.2$, and softer spectra with $Γ\approx 2.0$. A statistically significant positive correlation between $Γ$ and $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ is detected in RQ quasars, supporting disk--corona coupling models. To validate our results within the broader context of AGN evolution, we further examine the dependence of $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ on redshift ($z$) and black hole mass ($M_{\mathrm{BH}}$). For RQ quasars, $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ increases with redshift and decreases with $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$, in strong agreement with recent results \cite{aggarwal2024evidence}, highlighting the universal nature of these accretion trends. By correlating spectral slope with accretion rate, this work provides new insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and the cosmic evolution of quasars.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 642 quasars from XMM-Newton and SDSS data reveals that radio-quiet quasars exhibit a positive correlation between photon index (Γ) and Eddington ratio (λ_Edd), supporting disk-corona coupling models, with λ_Edd increasing with redshift and decreasing with black hole mass.
AI.motivation: To establish and characterize the fundamental relationship between the photon index (Γ) and Eddington ratio (λ_Edd) for the radio-quiet quasar population, and to validate these results within the broader context of AGN evolution.
AI.method: Cross-matched XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalog (DR11) with SDSS (DR16) quasar catalog; stringent quality filtering; automated spectral reduction; derived photon indices and intrinsic X-ray luminosities; classified 561 RQ and 81 RL quasars; estimated bolometric luminosity and Eddington ratio from X-ray and virial black hole mass measurements.
AI.result: RQ quasars show systematically higher Eddington ratios (peak at log λ_Edd ≈ -1.2) and softer spectra (Γ ≈ 2.0); a significant positive correlation between Γ and λ_Edd is found in RQ quasars; λ_Edd increases with redshift and decreases with M_BH for RQ quasars.
AI.conclusion: The positive Γ–λ_Edd correlation supports disk-corona coupling models; the redshift and mass dependencies of λ_Edd align with recent results, highlighting universal accretion trends and providing insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and cosmic quasar evolution.

title: A Review on Resolving the Hubble Tension via Late-Universe Physics
summary: The $Λ$CDM cosmological model has been successful in explaining many astronomical observations. However, recent observations increasingly point to deviations from the standard $Λ$CDM framework. Among these, one of the most significant discrepancies is the \textit{Hubble tension}, which refers to the difference in values obtained for the Hubble constant $H_0$ from high-redshift measurement and local observation. To address this issue, numerous cosmological models and methodological approaches have been proposed. This review offers a concise overview of recent progress in resolving the Hubble tension. The combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) and uncalibrated Type Ia supernovae data yields a value for $H_0$ that is significantly higher than the $Λ$CDM predication based on early-universe probes, even without incorporating local distance ladder constraints. This result indicates that the origin of the Hubble tension lies in new physics at low redshifts. Our findings suggest that although many unresolved systematics persist in current observations, they are insufficient to account for the magnitude of the current Hubble tension. This implies the likely existence of new physical mechanisms that have yet to be discovered.

AI.tldr: This review examines the Hubble tension—the discrepancy between high-redshift and local measurements of the Hubble constant H0—and finds that even without local distance ladder data, DESI BAO + uncalibrated Type Ia supernovae yield H0 values higher than ΛCDM predictions, suggesting new low-redshift physics beyond systematic errors is needed to resolve the tension.
AI.motivation: The Hubble tension represents one of the most significant discrepancies in modern cosmology, challenging the standard ΛCDM model. The authors aim to review recent progress and determine whether systematics or new physics are responsible.
AI.method: The review analyzes the combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) data with uncalibrated Type Ia supernovae to measure H0, without relying on local distance ladder constraints.
AI.result: The DESI BAO + uncalibrated supernovae combination yields an H0 value significantly higher than the ΛCDM prediction from early-universe probes, even excluding local distance ladder data. Current unresolved systematics are insufficient to explain the magnitude of the tension.
AI.conclusion: The origin of the Hubble tension lies in new physics at low redshifts, implying the likely existence of undiscovered physical mechanisms beyond the standard ΛCDM framework.

title: The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation and the high-mass end of the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Using a sample of 151 galaxies with dynamically measured black hole (BH) masses ($M_{\rm BH}$), we investigate the scaling relations between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the stellar velocity dispersion, $σ$, and, for a subsample of 30 core-Sérsic galaxies, between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the size of the partially depleted core, $R_{\rm b}$. Core-Sérsic galaxies, identified using high-resolution $Hubble ~ Space ~ Telescope$ imaging and spanning both the normal-core $(R_{\rm b}<0.5$ kpc) and large-core ($R_{\rm b}>0.5$ kpc) regimes, define an updated $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation of the form $M_{\rm BH} \propto R_{\rm b}^{1.16 \pm 0.10}$, with an rms scatter of $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.28$ dex in $\log M_{\rm BH}$. We find that Sérsic and normal-core galaxies together follow a common log-linear $M_{\rm BH}$-$σ$ relation with a slope of $4.95 \pm 0.29$ and a scatter $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.46$ dex. Deviations from this relation arise at the highest BH masses, where large-core galaxies, including six with direct $M_{\rm BH}$ measurements, drive a significant upturn. We find that these galaxies typically host ultramassive black holes whose masses scale more strongly with $R_{\rm b}$ than $σ$, and lie $\sim (1-4$) $~\times$ the intrinsic scatter (0.39 dex) above the relation defined by Sérsic and normal-core galaxies. The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation shows $\sim 30$-$47\%$ less scatter in $\log M_{\rm BH}$ than the corresponding $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation for the same sample. We interpret the high-mass upturn in the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ diagram as a consequence of successive major, dry mergers, a scenario that naturally explains the observed flattening of the $σ-L_V$ relation at $M_V < -23.5$ mag.

AI.tldr: This study examines scaling relations between black hole mass and galaxy properties using 151 galaxies, finding that core-Sérsic galaxies (especially those with large cores) host ultramassive black holes that deviate from standard M_BH-σ relations, and that M_BH scales more tightly with core size (R_b) than velocity dispersion (σ), with the high-mass upturn explained by dry mergers.
AI.motivation: To improve understanding of black hole-galaxy coevolution by investigating scaling relations between dynamically measured BH masses and both stellar velocity dispersion (σ) and core size (R_b), particularly for core-Sérsic galaxies which may host the most massive black holes.
AI.method: Analyzed a sample of 151 galaxies with dynamically measured BH masses; identified core-Sérsic galaxies using high-resolution HST imaging; divided core-Sérsic galaxies into normal-core (R_b<0.5 kpc) and large-core (R_b>0.5 kpc) regimes; fitted M_BH-σ and M_BH-R_b scaling relations; compared scatter between relations.
AI.result: M_BH ∝ R_b^{1.16±0.10} with scatter ~0.28 dex for core-Sérsic galaxies; M_BH-σ relation for Sérsic+normal-core galaxies has slope 4.95±0.29 with scatter ~0.46 dex; large-core galaxies with ultramassive BHs lie ~1-4× intrinsic scatter above this relation; M_BH-R_b shows 30-47% less scatter than M_BH-σ.
AI.conclusion: The high-mass upturn in M_BH-σ is likely due to successive major dry mergers, which also explains the flattening of σ-L_V relation at M_V<-23.5 mag; core size is a tighter predictor of BH mass than velocity dispersion for the most massive galaxies.

title: Machine Learning Does It and Does It Better: Unearthing Primordial Dark-Matter Velocities from the Matter Power Spectrum
summary: One effective way of learning about the production and properties of dark matter in the early universe is by extracting information about the primordial dark-matter phase-space distribution from the matter power spectrum. Several years ago a simple empirical formula was introduced which successfully reproduces most of the salient features of the primordial dark-matter phase-space distribution from the matter power spectrum -- even in situations in which this distribution is non-thermal, multi-modal, or exhibits other complicated features. Continuing this line of research, we investigate the extent to which machine-learning techniques can improve upon this analytic approach. Interestingly, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional neural network not only succeeds in reconstructing the dark-matter phase-space distribution with greater accuracy, but can also be applied to a broader range of matter power spectra.

AI.tldr: A 1D convolutional neural network reconstructs primordial dark-matter phase-space distributions from the matter power spectrum more accurately and across a broader range than the previous empirical analytic formula.
AI.motivation: To improve upon an existing empirical formula for extracting the primordial dark-matter phase-space distribution from the matter power spectrum, especially for non-thermal, multi-modal, or complex distributions.
AI.method: Applied a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) to reconstruct the dark-matter phase-space distribution from the matter power spectrum, and compared its performance to the earlier analytic empirical formula.
AI.result: The 1D CNN reconstructs the phase-space distribution with greater accuracy than the analytic formula and can be applied to a broader range of matter power spectra.
AI.conclusion: Machine-learning techniques, specifically 1D CNNs, offer a significant improvement over analytic methods for inferring primordial dark-matter properties from cosmological observables.

title: Unprecedented Constraints on Gas Flows at High Redshift Using Deep JWST/NIRSpec Observations from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA Surveys
comment: 31 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We investigate how low-ionization gas flows in typical star-forming galaxies at $z\sim3$ depend on galaxy intrinsic properties and viewing angle. For this analysis we use JWST/NIRSpec observations of rest-frame near-UV Fe II and Mg II absorption, and rest-frame optical Na D absorption. This study combines galaxies from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA surveys and contains 176, 197, and 315 galaxies, respectively, with Fe II, Mg II, and Na D coverage. Based on both individual and composite spectra, we find no statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties. However, galaxies with detected outflows tend towards higher stellar masses, SFR, and $Σ_{\rm SFR}$ than those without outflows, suggesting that the two samples are not drawn from the same parent population. Finally, we additionally find that Mg II emission is preferentially detected in galaxies with lower stellar mass and $A_V$, and higher sSFR, consistent with conditions that favor the escape of resonantly scattered line and ionizing continuum radiation.
