We present the first evidence in $z\sim3$ star-forming galaxies that properties of the absorption lines depend on galaxy inclination, with more face-on systems showing stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities, while inflowing gas is more frequently detected in more highly inclined galaxies. These trends are consistent with observations at $z\lesssim1$ and predictions from cosmological simulations in which galactic winds are launched perpendicular to the galactic disks, while accretion occurs primarily along the disk plane.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes low-ionization gas outflows and inflows in z~3 star-forming galaxies using JWST/NIRSpec observations of Fe II, Mg II, and Na D absorption. While outflow velocity shows no significant correlation with galaxy properties, galaxies with detected outflows tend to be more massive and star-forming. Mg II emission favors low-mass, low-dust, high-sSFR galaxies. First evidence at z~3 shows inclination-dependent absorption: face-on galaxies exhibit stronger outflows, while edge-on galaxies show more inflowing gas, consistent with disk-perpendicular wind and disk-plane accretion scenarios.
AI.motivation: To understand how low-ionization gas flows in high-redshift (z~3) star-forming galaxies depend on intrinsic galaxy properties and viewing angle, leveraging JWST's unprecedented sensitivity to probe rest-frame near-UV and optical absorption lines.
AI.method: Analysis of JWST/NIRSpec observations of rest-frame near-UV Fe II and Mg II absorption, and rest-frame optical Na D absorption from 176, 197, and 315 galaxies across the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA surveys, using individual and composite spectra.
AI.result: No statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties were found; galaxies with outflows tend toward higher stellar masses, SFR, and Σ_SFR. Mg II emission preferentially detected in lower stellar mass, lower A_V, higher sSFR galaxies. First evidence at z~3 shows face-on systems have stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities, while inflowing gas is more frequently detected in highly inclined galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Galactic winds at z~3 are launched perpendicular to galactic disks, while accretion occurs primarily along the disk plane, consistent with lower-redshift observations and cosmological simulations.

title: A local Universe catalogue of structures and voids dynamically identified using Cosmic-Flows4++ZOA peculiar velocities
summary: Cosmic voids and superclusters are among the largest structures in the Universe and provide complementary probes of the growth of large-scale structure and the underlying gravitational field. We present a comprehensive catalogue of the main local Universe cosmic web voids and knots, using the updated CosmicFlows-4++ Zone of Avoidance (CF4++ZOA) catalogue out to redshift z=0.1. To do this we use the V-web algorithm which provides a dynamically motivated map of the the local cosmic web, tracing the major expanding and converging regions of the local Universe. The robustness of the catalogue is assessed using the ensemble of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo realizations of the CF4++ZOA reconstruction. We additionally remove any structure that exceeds the survey boundaries and present catalogues of 37 voids and 42 knot regions within the reconstructed survey volume. The identified emptying regions (voids) have effective radii ranging from 13 to 38 h-1Mpc. The high density converging regions (knots) have volumes ranging from 10^4 to 3.3x10^5 h-3 Mpc^3.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a comprehensive catalogue of 37 cosmic voids and 42 supercluster knots in the local Universe (z<0.1) using the CF4++ZOA survey and V-web algorithm, with effective void radii of 13-38 h⁻¹Mpc and knot volumes of 10⁴-3.3×10⁵ h⁻³Mpc³.
AI.motivation: Cosmic voids and superclusters are among the largest structures in the Universe and provide complementary probes of the growth of large-scale structure and the underlying gravitational field. A comprehensive catalogue of these structures in the local Universe is needed for such studies.
AI.method: The authors use the V-web algorithm applied to the CosmicFlows-4++ Zone of Avoidance (CF4++ZOA) catalogue out to redshift z=0.1, with robustness assessed via an ensemble of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo realizations of the reconstruction. Structures exceeding survey boundaries are removed.
AI.result: Catalogues of 37 voids (effective radii 13-38 h⁻¹Mpc) and 42 knot regions (volumes 10⁴-3.3×10⁵ h⁻³Mpc³) within the reconstructed survey volume.
AI.conclusion: The V-web algorithm provides a dynamically motivated map of the local cosmic web, tracing major expanding (voids) and converging (knots) regions of the local Universe, with the catalogue validated through Monte Carlo realizations.

title: Supermassive Black Hole Assembly from Heavy Seeds with Dynamical Friction in the BRAHMA Simulations: Implications for JWST, LISA, and the Local Universe
summary: The JWST discoveries of supermassive black holes (BHs) at $z \gtrsim 5$ may provide key insights into their seeding origins. Using new $[18{-}72~\rm Mpc]^3$ BRAHMA cosmological simulations, we investigate how variations in heavy-seed prescriptions, coupled with a subgrid dynamical friction model, shape BH populations at $z \sim 5$ and $z \sim 0$. We consider two "lenient'' seed models, in which all halos containing sufficient dense & metal-poor gas form $\sim10^4$ and $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds, and a "strict'' seed model, in which $\sim10^5 M_{\odot}$ seeds form only under additional constraints motivated by direct collapse black hole formation. By $z \sim 5$, all models produce $M_*-M_{\rm BH}$ relations broadly consistent with the observed local Universe for $M_*\gtrsim10^9~M_{\odot}$ galaxies, but only the lenient scenarios generate systems near the upper envelope of the observed local scatter. In galaxies hosting $M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^8$-$10^9~M_{\odot}$ BHs, lenient production of $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds also produces multiple overmassive systems with $M_{\rm BH}/M_* \gtrsim 0.01$. Although their growth is dominated by seeding and mergers, these systems reach luminosities of $\sim10^{43}$-$10^{45}\mathrm{erg s^{-1}}$, comparable to those inferred for JWST-detected BHs. As a key observational signature, the lenient seed models yield merger rates of $\gtrsim100\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and near-unity local BH occupation fractions even in galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^7~M_{\odot}$. In contrast, the strict seed model produces merger rates of only $\sim1\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and local occupation fractions of $\lesssim10\%$ for galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^8~M_{\odot}$. Future gravitational-wave event rates and measurements of local BH occupation fractions will therefore provide strong constraints on the dominant pathways responsible for high-redshift BH assembly.

AI.tldr: Using BRAHMA cosmological simulations, this study shows that lenient (heavy) seed models for supermassive black holes produce populations consistent with JWST-detected BHs at z~5, with high merger rates (~100/yr) and near-unity occupation fractions in low-mass galaxies, whereas strict seed models yield low merger rates (~1/yr) and low occupation fractions, offering observational discriminants for seeding pathways.
AI.motivation: To understand the seeding origins of supermassive black holes discovered by JWST at z≳5 by testing how different heavy-seed prescriptions (lenient vs. strict) affect BH populations at high and low redshift.
AI.method: BRAHMA cosmological simulations ([18–72 Mpc]^3) with a subgrid dynamical friction model, comparing two lenient seed models (~10^4 and ~10^5 M⊙ seeds in halos with dense, metal-poor gas) and a strict seed model (~10^5 M⊙ seeds with additional direct collapse BH constraints).
AI.result: All models match local M_*-M_BH relations at M_*≳10^9 M⊙, but only lenient models produce overmassive systems (M_BH/M_*≳0.01) at z~5 with luminosities ~10^43-10^45 erg/s. Lenient models yield merger rates >100/yr and near-unity occupation fractions in galaxies with M_*≲10^7 M⊙; strict models yield ~1/yr merger rates and <10% occupation fractions for M_*≲10^8 M⊙.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational-wave event rates and measurements of local BH occupation fractions can strongly constrain the dominant BH seeding pathways responsible for high-redshift assembly.

title: SIDM and CDM interpretations of the million-solar-mass lensing perturber JVAS B1938+666-$\mathcal{V}$
summary: A $10^6\,M_\odot$ object has recently been inferred from gravitational imaging of the strong-lensing system JVAS B1938+666, exhibiting an unusually dense inner region embedded within an extended envelope, far exceeding expectations for cold dark matter (CDM) halos. Using gravothermal fluid simulations, we show that such a structure arises naturally in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos evolving into a deep core-collapse phase, where a secondary dense central core forms within an extended profile. The resulting density structure closely matches the inferred properties of the lensing object. We also demonstrate that a similar profile could be reproduced in CDM in the presence of an intermediate-mass black hole, but this requires an early-forming progenitor that subsequently loses $5$ orders of magnitude in mass through tidal stripping by the lens galaxy. Whether such a scenario can be realized in realistic cosmological environments remains an open question.

AI.tldr: A study shows that an ultra-dense dark matter object inferred from gravitational lensing JVAS B1938+666 can be naturally explained by self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) undergoing core collapse, whereas a cold dark matter (CDM) explanation requires an intermediate-mass black hole with extreme tidal stripping—an unlikely scenario.
AI.motivation: To explain the unexpectedly dense dark matter structure observed in the strong-lensing system JVAS B1938+666, which challenges standard CDM predictions.
AI.method: Gravothermal fluid simulations of SIDM halos to model core-collapse evolution, and comparison with a CDM + intermediate-mass black hole scenario.
AI.result: The SIDM core-collapse model naturally reproduces the inferred dense inner core + extended envelope structure of the lensing object. The CDM + IMBH scenario can also reproduce the profile but requires extreme fine-tuning (early progenitor, ~5 orders of magnitude mass loss via tidal stripping).
AI.conclusion: The observed object is consistent with a SIDM halo in deep core collapse, while the CDM alternative is physically plausible but cosmologically unlikely.

title: Direct detection of cool molecular gas in a star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Main text: 17 pages, 6 figures
summary: We investigate the molecular gas content and interstellar medium (ISM) conditions of REBELS-25, a massive, star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$. Deep VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations reveal CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) emission (both at $\sim3.5σ$), and provide an upper limit on [C I](2-1). From the CMB-corrected CO(3-2) flux-representing the highest-redshift detection of a low-$J$ CO transition to date-we derive a molecular gas mass of $M_{\rm mol}=(1.0\pm0.4)\times10^{11}\,(α_{\rm CO}/(3\,$M$_{\odot}$(K$\,$\kms$\,$pc$^2)^{-1}))\,$M$_{\odot}$, directly confirming the presence of a very massive gas reservoir only $\simeq700\,$Myr after the Big Bang. This implies an extreme gas fraction of $f_{\rm gas}\simeq0.95$, a gas-to-dust ratio of $δ_{\rm GDR}\simeq6\times10^2$, and a depletion timescale of $τ_{\rm dep}\simeq1.2\,$Gyr, broadly consistent with extrapolated scaling relations for main-sequence galaxies at lower redshift. Using the radiative transfer code TUNER, we self-consistently model CO and dust continuum emission in the context of the significant CMB background, constraining ISM properties and recovering $M_{\rm mol}= (1.8^{+1.0}_{-0.9})\times10^{11}\,$M$_{\odot}$, independent of assumptions about $r_{31}$ and $α_{\rm CO}$. We further discuss the use of alternative molecular gas tracers at early epochs. Combining CO and [C II] measurements, we infer an empirical [C II]-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $α_{\rm [C II]}=(60\pm25)\,$M$_{\odot}$/L$_{\odot}$, suggesting [C II] remains a viable molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization. These results demonstrate the detectability of low-$J$ CO emission even at $z>7$, paving the way for next-generation facilities, and provide critical insights into the rapid mass assembly of galaxies during the first billion years of cosmic history.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the detection of CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) emission from REBELS-25, a massive star-forming galaxy at z=7.31, confirming a massive molecular gas reservoir (~10¹¹ M☉) only ~700 Myr after the Big Bang, with an extreme gas fraction (~0.95) and long depletion timescale (~1.2 Gyr). Using radiative transfer modeling and multi-tracer analysis, the study constrains ISM properties and validates [C II] as a viable molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.motivation: To investigate the molecular gas content and ISM conditions of REBELS-25, a massive star-forming galaxy at z=7.31, in order to understand how galaxies assemble gas and form stars in the early Universe.
AI.method: Deep VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations targeting CO(3-2), CO(7-6), and [C I](2-1) emission; radiative transfer modeling with TUNER to self-consistently model CO and dust continuum under CMB background; multi-tracer analysis combining CO, [C II], and dust measurements.
AI.result: Detected CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) at ~3.5σ, with CO(3-2) being the highest-redshift detection of a low-J CO transition. Derived molecular gas mass M_mol=(1.0±0.4)×10¹¹ (α_CO/3) M☉; radiative transfer yields M_mol=(1.8^+1.0_-0.9)×10¹¹ M☉. Inferred gas fraction ~0.95, gas-to-dust ratio ~6×10², depletion timescale ~1.2 Gyr. Empirical [C II]-to-H₂ conversion factor α_[C II]=(60±25) M☉/L☉.
AI.conclusion: Low-J CO emission is detectable at z>7, confirming a massive gas reservoir in the early Universe. The galaxy is gas-rich with long depletion timescale, consistent with scaled relations of lower-z main-sequence galaxies. [C II] remains a viable molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization. Results pave the way for next-generation facilities studying early galaxy assembly.

title: Chemical signatures from the first stars embedded in metal-poor gas in galaxies at cosmic dawn
summary: The first generation of stars formed from pristine, neutral hydrogen gas. The most massive of these exploded as supernovae within a few million years of their birth, producing the first heavier elements and leaving distinct chemical signatures of their origin in the surrounding medium. However, chemical abundance studies have so far mainly relied on emission-line measurements, which are luminosity weighted and hence biased towards the most recently formed stars. Here we analyse near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program of three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8, 8.6, and 9.3, within the first 650 to 520 million years after the Big Bang. The chemical abundance patterns of the metal lines detected in absorption hint at extremely metal-poor gas, substantially lower than inferred from the emission lines tracing the central, star-forming regions. Further, they all exhibit super-solar [C/O] abundances, which is also imprinted in the averaged spectrum of a larger set of galaxies at similar redshifts. These results reveal the distinct chemical signatures of the first Population III supernovae explosions.

AI.tldr: JWST-SPURS observations of three UV-bright galaxies at z=7.8-9.3 reveal extremely metal-poor gas with super-solar [C/O] abundances from absorption lines, distinct from emission-line measurements, providing evidence of chemical signatures from the first Population III supernovae.
AI.motivation: Previous chemical abundance studies relied on emission-line measurements, which are biased towards recently formed stars. The authors aimed to overcome this limitation by analyzing absorption-line spectroscopy to detect the pristine chemical signatures of the first stars (Population III) in the early universe.
AI.method: Near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program was used to analyze absorption lines in three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8, 8.6, and 9.3 (520-650 million years post-Big Bang). The absorption-line chemical abundances were compared to emission-line measurements, and an averaged spectrum of a larger galaxy sample at similar redshifts was also examined.
AI.result: The absorption lines reveal extremely metal-poor gas, significantly lower than inferred from emission lines tracing central star-forming regions. All three galaxies exhibit super-solar [C/O] abundances, a signature also seen in the averaged spectrum of a larger galaxy sample at similar redshifts.
AI.conclusion: These absorption-line chemical abundance patterns reveal the distinct chemical signatures of the first Population III supernovae explosions, providing direct evidence of the earliest stellar generations in the universe.

title: Grain Alignment and Dust Evolution Physics with Polarisation (GRADE-POL). II. On the physical basis of Serkowski and super-Serkowski polarisation spectra
summary: Optical-to-near infrared interstellar polarisation, induced by aligned dust grains, generally follows a convex wavelength dependence, known as the Serkowski relation. However, observations in the ultraviolet (UV) and at [mid-]infrared wavelengths indicated that some of the spectra do not follow this relation. Specifically, about 25% show an excess in the degree of polarisation at mid-UV wavelengths ($λ^{-1} > 3\,\rm μm^{-1}$), referred to as the super-Serkowski polarisation. In this study, we re-examine both the Serkowski and super-Serkowski spectra based on the joint effect of paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment. We used the observational data for HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903 and HD 161056 to constrain our modelling. We examined two types of radiation fields: one derived from the scaled interstellar radiation field and another originating from a B-type star. For the super-Serkowski spectra of HD 30614 and HD 204827, our model demonstrates that RAT alignment enhanced by radiation produced from a B-type star below the Lyman limit ($λ=912 Å$) can reasonably explain the observations and that a combination with the DG alignments results in a better fit for $λ^{-1}\geq 5.5\,\rm μm^{-1}$. For the Serkowski spectra in HD 37903 and HD 161056, only RAT alignment by itself under the typical interstellar radiation field above the Lyman limit, within a typical cold neutral medium, can account for the observed spectra, with a combination of a very inefficient DG alignment. The capacity of our model to predict the starlight polarisation spectrum up to from infrared to far-UV is thus a promising tool for interpreting future missions that observe spectrophotometry in the UV bands.

AI.tldr: This paper models interstellar polarisation spectra (Serkowski and super-Serkowski types) using paramagnetic relaxation (DG) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment mechanisms. The super-Serkowski excess in HD 30614 and HD 204827 is explained by RAT alignment from B-type star radiation below the Lyman limit, with DG contributing at higher wavenumbers. Serkowski spectra in HD 37903 and HD 161056 require only RAT alignment under typical interstellar radiation above the Lyman limit, with minimal DG alignment.
AI.motivation: About 25% of interstellar polarisation spectra show a UV excess (super-Serkowski) deviating from the canonical Serkowski relation. The physical origin of this excess was unclear, motivating a re-examination using joint DG and RAT alignment mechanisms to explain both normal and anomalous polarisation spectra.
AI.method: The authors modelled polarisation spectra for four stars (HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903, HD 161056) using two alignment mechanisms: paramagnetic relaxation (DG) and radiative torque (RAT). They tested two radiation field types (scaled interstellar radiation field and B-star radiation) and compared model predictions to observational data across UV to near-IR wavelengths.
AI.result: Super-Serkowski spectra (HD 30614, HD 204827) are best explained by RAT alignment from B-star radiation below the Lyman limit (912 Å), with added DG alignment improving fits at λ⁻¹ ≥ 5.5 μm⁻¹. Serkowski spectra (HD 37903, HD 161056) require only RAT alignment under typical interstellar radiation above the Lyman limit in a cold neutral medium, with very inefficient DG alignment.
AI.conclusion: The combined DG+RAT alignment model successfully reproduces both normal and anomalous interstellar polarisation spectra from infrared to far-UV, offering a promising tool for interpreting future UV spectrophotometric missions.

title: Beyond the Fundamental Metallicity Relation: galaxy sizes encode the link between inflow and metallicity
comment: 25 pages, 23 figures. Resubmitted to MNRAS after moderate revisions
summary: Gas-phase chemical abundances are key observable consequences of galaxy evolution, being intrinsically tied to galaxy formation histories. Gas metallicity rises with increasing stellar mass ($\mathrm{M_*}$), forming the well-known mass-metallicity relation (MZR). MZR residuals have separately been shown to anti-correlate with star-formation rate (the ``fundamental'' metallicity relation), with gas mass and with optical size, but no single analysis has considered all trends together. We thus perform a combined analysis of all three trends, utilizing optical MaNGA integral field spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses. We estimate inner gas masses for $\sim$1500 star-forming galaxies, finding this to be the most important parameter after $\mathrm{M_*}$ in predicting gas metallicities. We obtain equivalent results for stellar metallicities and gaseous N/O, suggesting that current inner gas masses are intrinsically linked to long-term chemical evolution histories. We show that more compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses, challenging suggestions that deeper gravitational potentials confer higher metallicities. We find a strong correlation between inner gas mass and galaxy size, meaning that short term inflow fluctuations cannot be responsible for the MZR residuals. With chemical evolution models, we show that our results can instead be explained by differences in long-term inflow histories. The earlier inflow histories of compact galaxies lead to lower gas masses and more rapidly declining gas reservoirs at late times, leading to higher metallicities. At fixed stellar mass, galaxy size therefore encodes the link between halo assembly histories, long-term gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs and metallicity.

AI.tldr: Using MaNGA and HI-MaNGA data for ~1500 galaxies, this study shows that inner gas mass is the most important secondary parameter (after stellar mass) in predicting gas-phase metallicities, and that galaxy size encodes long-term inflow histories—compact galaxies had earlier inflow, lower gas masses, and higher metallicities.
AI.motivation: To perform a combined analysis of the three known residual trends in the mass-metallicity relation (MZR residuals with star-formation rate, gas mass, and optical size) that had not been studied together, and to understand the physical origin of these correlations.
AI.method: Combined analysis of optical MaNGA integral field spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses for ~1500 star-forming galaxies; chemical evolution modeling to interpret the observed trends.
AI.result: Inner gas mass is the most important secondary parameter after M* for predicting gas metallicities; compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses (challenging the deeper-potential explanation); a strong correlation between inner gas mass and galaxy size rules out short-term inflow fluctuations; the results are explained by differences in long-term inflow histories.
AI.conclusion: At fixed stellar mass, galaxy size encodes the link between halo assembly histories, long-term gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs, and metallicity—earlier inflow in compact galaxies leads to lower gas masses and higher metallicities.

title: Basis sets and Coulomb resolutions in rotational coordinates
comment: Author-accepted manuscript; see J. Phys. A for final published version
summary: Using generalised Laplacian symmetry operators, we construct basis sets or Coulomb resolutions in several separable coordinate systems, including two R-separable systems. This expands the possible geometries in which basis set construction is feasible, a problem which is relevant to both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry. In particular we derive three basis sets (two in prolate spheroidal and one in cylindrical coordinates) which are expressible in closed-form using a single Jacobi polynomial. We also show how any spherical polar or prolate spheroidal basis set may be transformed into a bispherical or toroidal basis set.

AI.tldr: This paper develops new basis sets for Coulomb problems in separable coordinate systems (prolate spheroidal, cylindrical, bispherical, toroidal) using generalized Laplacian symmetry operators, with closed-form expressions involving Jacobi polynomials.
AI.motivation: To expand the range of coordinate geometries where basis set construction is feasible for Coulomb problems, relevant to both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.
AI.method: Generalised Laplacian symmetry operators are used to construct basis sets in separable coordinate systems, including two R-separable systems. Closed-form basis sets are derived using a single Jacobi polynomial in prolate spheroidal and cylindrical coordinates. Transformation rules from spherical polar/prolate spheroidal to bispherical/toroidal bases are also provided.
AI.result: Three closed-form basis sets were derived: two in prolate spheroidal coordinates and one in cylindrical coordinates, all expressible via a single Jacobi polynomial. Additionally, a transformation method from spherical polar or prolate spheroidal basis sets to bispherical or toroidal basis sets was demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: The work expands the set of coordinate systems available for Coulomb basis set construction, enabling new geometries for applications in galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.

title: Galaxy clusters in the VIDEO fields: detection and characterisation in the context of MOONRISE
summary: We analyse the cluster content of the $\sim 4.5 \text{ deg}^{2}$ XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields which are expected to be partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey. Using AMICO and WaZP photometric redshift-based cluster finders, we construct a sample of $519$ cluster candidates detected by both finders in the redshift range $z = 0.1-3$, including $74$ detections at $z > 1.5$. For all detections, we identify the Brightest Central Galaxy (BCG) and compute a list of probabilistic cluster memberships. Our photometric redshift measurements of the clusters agree well with spectroscopic redshifts from the literature, when available. From ancillary spectroscopic data, we assign $z_\text{spec}$ measurements to $116$ cluster candidates based on their spectroscopic members and to $204$ based on their likely BCGs. We also show that candidates containing Radio-Loud members are efficiently recovered using the prior-based cluster finder PPM. We perform a preliminary analysis of the galaxy content of these candidates, focusing on the Red-Sequence components of their apparent Colour-Magnitude Diagram. By comparing with models of galaxy evolution, we show that this population is consistent with a model of passive evolution with a formation at high redshift, and is already in place at $z = 1.5-2.0$. Finally, our cluster sample is used to evaluate how these clusters would be detected and characterised, according to various MOONRISE strategies. We show that cluster spectroscopic confirmation and characterisation could be efficiently achieved up to $z\sim1.7$ even with the shallowest survey strategy. This open unprecedented insight into the physical properties of high-redshift galaxy clusters and into galaxy formation in dense environments.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes ~519 galaxy cluster candidates (74 at z>1.5) in the XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields using AMICO and WaZP cluster finders, validates them with spectroscopic data, studies their red-sequence evolution, and evaluates detectability under different MOONRISE survey strategies, finding efficient characterization up to z~1.7.
AI.motivation: To construct and validate a large sample of high-redshift galaxy cluster candidates in fields partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey, and to assess how different survey strategies would perform in detecting and characterizing these distant clusters.
AI.method: Used two photometric redshift-based cluster finders (AMICO and WaZP) on ~4.5 deg² of XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields; identified BCGs and computed probabilistic memberships; cross-matched with spectroscopic redshifts; applied the prior-based PPM finder for radio-loud member recovery; analyzed Colour-Magnitude Diagrams and compared with passive evolution models; simulated detection under various MOONRISE survey strategies.
AI.result: 519 cluster candidates detected by both finders (z=0.1-3), with 74 at z>1.5; spectroscopic redshifts assigned to 116 candidates via members and 204 via BCGs; red-sequence population consistent with passive evolution forming at high redshift, already in place at z=1.5-2.0; cluster confirmation feasible up to z~1.7 even with the shallowest MOONRISE strategy.
AI.conclusion: The cluster sample provides a robust benchmark for the MOONRISE survey, demonstrating that even shallow strategies enable efficient spectroscopic confirmation and characterization of high-redshift clusters, offering insights into galaxy formation in dense environments.

title: Feedback in Extragalactic Star Clusters (FEAST): Spectral Energy Distributions and the Physical Properties of Star Clusters in NGC 628 with CIGALE
summary: With Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of NGC~628 spanning 0.3--7.7\,$μ$m, we fit the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of over 12,000 optically-selected star clusters, emerging young star clusters (eYSCs), and MIRI-selected sources with \textsc{cigale} to derive their ages, masses, extinctions, and dust properties. We find that near-infrared selected eYSC-I (compact Pa$α$ and 3.3,$μ$m PAH emission) and eYSC-II (compact Pa$α$ and diffuse 3.3,$μ$m PAH emssion) sources peak at $\sim$3--5~Myr, where $\sim 12\%$ of the clusters have an $E(B{-}V)>2$, demonstrating the presence of dust-embedded populations as clusters emerge. Further, the distributions of the fractional polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) abundance ($q_{\mathrm PAH}$) and stellar-to-nebular attenuation ratio ($E(B{-}V)_{\rm \star}/E(B{-}V)_{\rm neb}$) suggest an evolutionary sequence in which sources evolve from eYSC-I to eYSC-II as clusters clear their surrounding dust and gas. The photo-dissociation region (PDR) clearing timescale inferred from the ratio of eYSC-I to optically visible stellar clusters is $\sim$4~Myr. Additionally, we find that star clusters in the spiral arms of NGC 628 are preferentially more massive and more dust-reddened than those in inter-arm regions.~Finally, we find that $\sim$65\% of eYSC-I, $\sim$27\% of eYSC-II, and $\sim$40\% of F335M-selected sources coincide with an F770W peak in our MIRI-selected catalog within 4 pixels, confirming that F770W-bright sources preferentially trace the youngest and dustiest regions. Overall, our results highlight the ability of JWST together with \textsc{cigale} model grids to identify and characterize eYSCs during their short-lived embedded phases, and provide constraints on the feedback mechanisms that govern the emergence of stellar clusters.

AI.tldr: Using HST and JWST observations of NGC 628, the study fits SEDs of over 12,000 star clusters to derive ages, masses, extinctions, and dust properties. eYSC-I and eYSC-II sources peak at ~3–5 Myr, with ~12% having E(B-V)>2, showing dust-embedded populations. An evolutionary sequence from eYSC-I to eYSC-II is inferred via PAH abundance and attenuation ratios, with a PDR clearing timescale of ~4 Myr. Spiral arm clusters are more massive and dust-reddened. ~65% of eYSC-I, ~27% of eYSC-II, and ~40% of F335M-selected sources coincide with F770W peaks, highlighting JWST's ability to characterize embedded young star clusters.
AI.motivation: To understand the early, dust-embedded phases of star cluster evolution and the feedback mechanisms that govern cluster emergence, using the combined capabilities of HST and JWST to probe previously obscured populations.
AI.method: SED fitting of over 12,000 sources (star clusters, eYSCs, MIRI-selected sources) in NGC 628 using CIGALE, with multi-wavelength data spanning 0.3–7.7 μm from HST and JWST. Sources were classified into eYSC-I (compact Paα and 3.3 μm PAH), eYSC-II (compact Paα and diffuse 3.3 μm PAH), and optically-selected clusters.
AI.result: eYSC-I and eYSC-II peak at ~3–5 Myr; ~12% of clusters have E(B-V)>2. Evolutionary sequence from eYSC-I to eYSC-II inferred from qPAH and E(B-V)⋆/E(B-V)neb distributions. PDR clearing timescale ≈4 Myr. Spiral arm clusters are more massive and reddened. Coincidence rates with F770W peaks: 65% eYSC-I, 27% eYSC-II, 40% F335M-selected.
AI.conclusion: JWST combined with CIGALE modeling effectively identifies and characterizes young embedded star clusters, providing constraints on the clearing timescales and feedback processes during the emergence of stellar clusters.

title: The ultra low-frequency spectral properties of bright extended radio galaxies in the 3CRR catalogue
summary: Context. Active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets are fundamental drivers of galaxy evolution, injecting kinetic energy into their environments. The large-scale morphology and spectral properties of these radio galaxies are consequences of complex particle acceleration, energy loss, and absorption processes. While the shape of the synchrotron spectrum encodes the plasma's energetic history, understanding the physics of particle acceleration and duty cycles has historically been limited by a lack of well-resolved observations at ultra-low frequencies (< 100 MHz), where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are traced. Aims. This study aims to perform the first comprehensive multi-frequency analysis of bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz. The goal is to study electron acceleration mechanisms, accurately measure the low-frequency spectral shape, and constrain the injection index for a sample of Fanaroff-Riley (FR) I and II galaxies using spectral ageing models. Methods. Utilising new 58 MHz observations from the LOFAR Low Band Antenna (LBA) combined with LOFAR High Band Antenna (HBA; 144 MHz) and Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS, 887 MHz & 943.5 MHz & 1367.5 MHz) data, a sub-sample of 22 extended sources from the 3CRR catalogue was selected, requiring the largest angular size to be at least 2.5'. The analysis involves constructing detailed spectral index maps and utilising radio colour-colour diagrams to interpret spectral shapes and constrain ageing model parameters across the radio lobes. Results. This study presents the ultra-low frequency spectral index maps for this sample. For FR I galaxies, spectral indices range from ~0.5 near the core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to > 1.0 in the lobes. For FR II galaxies, hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5 - 0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first comprehensive multi-frequency analysis of 22 bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz using LOFAR LBA, HBA, and RACS data. By constructing spectral index maps and radio colour-colour diagrams, the authors investigate electron acceleration mechanisms and spectral ageing in FR I and II galaxies. FR I galaxies show spectral indices from ~0.5 near the core to >1.0 in lobes; FR II hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5–0.9), suggesting complex particle acceleration or absorption.
AI.motivation: AGN jets are fundamental drivers of galaxy evolution, but understanding particle acceleration and duty cycles has been limited by a lack of well-resolved ultra-low-frequency (<100 MHz) observations, where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are traced.
AI.method: Utilised 58 MHz LOFAR LBA, 144 MHz LOFAR HBA, and RACS (887, 943.5, 1367.5 MHz) data. Selected 22 extended sources (LAS ≥ 2.5') from the 3CRR catalogue. Constructed spectral index maps and radio colour-colour diagrams to constrain spectral ageing model parameters across radio lobes.
AI.result: Presented ultra-low-frequency spectral index maps for the sample. FR I galaxies: spectral indices ~0.5 near core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to >1.0 in lobes. FR II galaxies: hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5–0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects.
AI.conclusion: The multi-frequency approach down to 58 MHz enables accurate measurement of low-frequency spectral shapes and constraints on injection indices, revealing different acceleration/absorption behaviours between FR I and FR II galaxies.

title: Centrally concentrated star formation in young clusters II: Jet feedback
comment: Data products associated with this work will be made publicly available through the American Museum of Natural History Digital Library after the paper is accepted for publication
summary: Protostellar jets are one of the earliest forms of stellar feedback, but their impact on star formation and cluster assembly in centrally concentrated molecular clouds remains poorly understood. We study how protostellar jets affect the star formation efficiency, the temporal variability of star formation, star cluster structure, and the early dynamical state of centrally concentrated, newly forming star clusters using the Torch star cluster formation framework. We adopt a centrally concentrated initial cloud model with mass M = 2.5 x 10^3 solar masses and compare six pairs of simulations with and without protostellar jets, supplemented by one additional higher resolution pair of simulations. We analyze our simulations using global star formation diagnostics together with structural and dynamical measures of the stellar population. Models with jet feedback achieve star formation efficiencies of 12-16%, while the corresponding models without jets yield higher efficiencies of 19-33%. Jets also cause star formation to occur in discrete bursts rather than continuously, to produce more extended and substructured stellar systems, and to leave behind stellar populations that are less tightly bound and have higher virial parameters. In our centrally concentrated initial conditions, runs with jets form stellar systems that better reproduce the observed range of the projected structural parameter Q_2D in young clusters than runs without jets, indicating that protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel even in centrally concentrated clouds that regulates star formation efficiencies and shapes the emerging cluster structure.

AI.tldr: Protostellar jets reduce star formation efficiency (12-16% vs 19-33%), induce bursty star formation, create more extended/substructured clusters, and produce stellar populations with higher virial parameters. Jets help simulations better match observed young cluster structures (Q_2D), demonstrating their importance as early feedback in centrally concentrated clouds.
AI.motivation: Protostellar jets are a key early feedback mechanism, but their specific impact on star formation and cluster assembly in centrally concentrated molecular clouds is poorly understood.
AI.method: Used the Torch star cluster formation framework to simulate a centrally concentrated cloud (M = 2.5×10³ M☉), comparing six pairs of simulations with/without protostellar jets plus one higher-resolution pair. Analyzed global star formation diagnostics, structural measures, and dynamical properties of the stellar population.
AI.result: Jets lower SFE (12-16% vs 19-33%), induce discrete bursty star formation, produce more extended and substructured systems with higher virial parameters and less bound populations. Jet-included runs better reproduce observed Q_2D structural parameters of young clusters.
AI.conclusion: Protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel that regulates star formation efficiency and shapes the structure of emerging star clusters, even in centrally concentrated clouds.
